After a successful SASL bind with integrity protection (SSF > 0), a remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE). In FreeIPA and Red Hat Identity Management deployments, any domain user with a valid Kerberos ticket, enrolled host, or service account can trigger this vulnerability over the network. This flaw is independent of CVE-2025-14905, which patched schema.c only and did not modify sasl_io.c.

The Tutor LMS – eLearning and online course solution plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.0 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to permanently delete any comment they authored anywhere on the site — including regular post comments and lesson comments — along with all replies to those comments authored by any other user, including Administrators and Instructors.

The MailerLite – Signup forms (official) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'form_id' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.27 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires an administrator to approve a comment containing the malicious shortcode, after which any page rendering the Latest Comments block with excerpts enabled will trigger the injected script for all visitors.
Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Frisbii Frisbii Pay reepay-checkout-gateway allows Object Injection.This issue affects Frisbii Pay: from n/a before 1.8.20.
Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Drupal Content Synchronizer allows Object Injection. This issue affects Content Synchronizer versions: from 0.0.0 to 4.1.1.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ("Cross-site Scripting") vulnerability in Drupal Content Synchronizer allows Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). This issue affects Content Synchronizer versions: from 0.0.0 to 4.1.1.

Z80 Ultra is affected by an information disclosure vulnerability in service interfaces related to application scenarios. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may result in an impact on confidentiality.
Z80 Ultra product has an improper access control vulnerability in the game assistant module. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability may affect confidentiality and integrity.

A flaw was found in Keycloak's SAML brokering functionality. When Keycloak is configured as a client in a Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) setup, it fails to validate the `NotOnOrAfter` timestamp within the `SubjectConfirmationData`. This allows an attacker to delay the expiration of SAML responses, potentially extending the time a response is considered valid and leading to unexpected session durations or resource consumption.

The Newsletters plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to time-based blind SQL Injection via the 'instance[lists]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.18.2 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The wpmlgetlistfields AJAX handler performs only a nonce check with no capability check, and the required refreshfields nonce is emitted on every wp-admin page including /wp-admin/profile.php, making the endpoint trivially reachable by any authenticated Subscriber.

The Points Management System For Gamification, Ranks, Badges, and Loyalty Rewards Program – myCred plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'key' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.0.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the Link Clicks hook to be enabled and that the attacker, as a Subscriber-level user, can access any front-end page rendering the [mycred_link] shortcode, which localizes the nonce needed to reach the AJAX endpoint.

The Swift Performance Lite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'REQUEST_URI (gated by $_GET['force-cache'])' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.3.7.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload is planted via a single unauthenticated GET request to any URL with ?force-cache=1 and a URL-encoded HTML payload in the path, which the plugin decodes and creates as a literal filesystem directory name; the script fires the next time an administrator opens the Swift Performance dashboard.

The Hide My WP Ghost – Security & Firewall plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.0.15 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that the plugin's URL rewriting mode is active (hmwp_mode set to a non-default value) and that the attacker has one previously approved comment from the same author/email address, after which WordPress auto-approves the attack comment without moderator intervention.

The PublishPress Tag Groups: Stylish Displays For Your Tags and Categories plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'separator' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.0.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is possible because wp_kses_post applied on save treats HTML-entity-encoded payloads as inert text, but the plugin's own check_attributes() function calls html_entity_decode() on the separator value before passing it to unescaped output, reconstituting live markup at render time.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 13.7.0 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with Maintainer-role permissions to obtain another user's authenticated session cookie and gain unauthorized access to that user's account due to improper session storage handling in the dependency proxy authentication flow when a redirect-pending state was triggered.

The Hustle – Email Marketing, Lead Generation, Optins, Popups plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'import_file' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.8.14.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires an administrator to have first delegated the hustle_edit_module capability to a lower-privileged role via the plugin's built-in Permissions screen; without that delegation, the import endpoint rejects non-Administrator users at the capability check.

The Timetics – Appointment Booking Calendar & Scheduling System plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized modification of data and user account creation in versions up to, and including, 1.0.67 This is due to the public `POST /wp-json/timetics/v1/bookings` route being registered with `permission_callback => function () { return true; }` and the handler (`create_item()` → `save_bookings()` → `booking_appointment()`) passing the attacker-controlled `email` directly into `Customer::make()`, which (a) grants the `timetics-customer` role to any existing WordPress user matched by email — including administrators and staff — and overwrites that account's `first_name`/`last_name` user meta, and (b) calls `wp_insert_user()` with role `timetics-customer` when the email is new, regardless of the site's `users_can_register` setting. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to create arbitrary WordPress user accounts, assign the `timetics-customer` role to existing accounts (including administrators), and overwrite their profile metadata.

The Duplicate Post plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[custom][names][prefix]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the site owner to have enabled both 'User Level Permissions' for the Subscriber role and the 'Show reference to original item?' option, and the targeted administrator must view the edit screen of the chained copy post in the classic editor.

The AutomatorWP – No-Code Workflow Automation, Integration & Webhooks Plugin, now with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'post_field_conditions[0][field]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.1.2 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with administrator-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The vulnerability requires a two-step exploit: a crafted field value must first be stored via the wp_ajax_automatorwp_update_item_option AJAX endpoint, and then the target automation must be triggered to fire the vulnerable SQL query.

The Widgets for Social Photo Feed plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'widget-id' shortcode attribute of the [trustindex-feed] shortcode in versions up to, and including, 1.8.3 This is due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping in the registerWidget() function, which concatenates the raw shortcode attribute directly into a double-quoted JavaScript string literal that is then enqueued via wp_add_inline_script() and rendered in wp_footer/admin_footer. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The theme for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'metavalue (via wp-admin/post.php add_meta → post_meta key 'my_field')' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. A Contributor can store a raw script payload in a custom field on their own draft and cause it to execute in an administrator's or editor's authenticated browser session when they preview or publish the post.

The Enfold theme for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'templateName' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.3.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The AJAX save handler validates a nonce and requires only the edit_posts capability, meaning a Contributor can legitimately obtain the nonce from their own post-edit screen and store a malicious template name that subsequently fires in every privileged user's session.

The Maps Plugin using Google Maps for WordPress - WP Google Map plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to SQL Injection via the array keys of the `categories` entries parsed from an imported JSON file in versions up to, and including, 1.9.9 This is due to the wgm_handle_import() function sanitizing only the known-named VALUES (`name`, `icon`) of each category object while passing the attacker-controlled JSON object KEYS directly to `$wpdb->insert()`, which interpolates them as column names into the generated INSERT statement without escaping embedded backticks. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above (when the plugin's own 'Minimum Role for Map Editor' setting has been configured to 'Subscriber', one of five values the plugin's settings UI offers), to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database, including administrator password hashes.

The Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'upload-1 (the File Upload field's element_id)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This vulnerability is an incomplete fix for CVE-2024-1794; exploitation requires that the Forminator form's File Upload field is left at plugin defaults (no 'custom-files' restriction configured) and that the server maps no Content-Type to the .rtx extension — the default behavior of the Debian/Ubuntu Apache package used by the official WordPress Docker image and many shared hosts.

The MW WP Form plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in all versions up to, and including, 5.1.8 via the 'mw-wp-form_session_mw-wp-form-<FORM_ID>' parameter due to missing validation on a user controlled key. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to overwrite or delete arbitrary WordPress transients in wp_options — including core-managed transients such as wp_styles_for_blocks — enabling injection of attacker-controlled CSS into every front-end page and permanent anchoring of poisoned transient values that never re-expire. The plugin's CSRF check does not prevent exploitation because MW_WP_Form_Data::__construct() registers _save_to_session() on the PHP shutdown hook before the CSRF check runs, causing the transient write to fire even after wp_safe_redirect()+exit; the GET path via the [mwform_formkey] shortcode has no CSRF check at all.

An improper certificate validation vulnerability exists in ADM App Central, due to disabled peer verification within the set-used-server endpoint, enabling an unauthenticated Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacker to intercept HTTPS traffic, bypass TLS validation, and modify App Central server redirection settings to cause a persistent service outage for application updates without bypassing package signature verification.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

An improper TLS certificate validation vulnerability exists in the ADM online update service. An unauthenticated attacker capable of performing a Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attack against the device's firmware update connection can impersonate the update server using an untrusted TLS certificate and supply malicious update metadata. The attacker may cause a crafted firmware image to be installed and execute arbitrary code with root privileges when automatic firmware updates are enabled.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

An improper authorization vulnerability exists in the wallpaper component of ADM. An authenticated, low-privileged user can bypass shared-folder access controls by specifying an image path within a restricted share. The CGI processes the request with root privileges without enforcing the source share's access permissions, allowing the attacker to copy and retrieve images they are not authorized to access, resulting in unauthorized information disclosure.
Affected products and versions include: from ADM 4.1.0 through ADM 4.3.3.RY62 as well as from ADM 5.0.0 through ADM 5.1.4.RM62.

Reflected cross-site scripting in the versioned REST API documentation page in Checkmk versions 2.5.0 before 2.5.0p21 allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of a user who opens a crafted link, in the context of that user's Checkmk session. The API version segment of the documentation URL is inserted into the page without escaping, and the page is reachable without authentication.

Issue summary: Calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input length close to INT_MAX
may overflow the calculation of the encoded output size and write past the end
of the caller-supplied output buffer.

Impact summary: No path by which an attacker can trigger this has been
identified. An application that passes an input length near INT_MAX to
EVP_EncodeBlock() could suffer a heap buffer overflow, crashing or corrupting
its own memory, but it must itself supply such a length.

CWE: CWE-190: Integer Overflow or Wraparound

Description: EVP_EncodeBlock() base64-encodes a buffer of a caller-supplied
length into an output buffer that the caller allocates. The caller is expected
to reserve 4*((len+2)/3)+1 bytes. For input lengths close to INT_MAX, the
arithmetic that computes the encoded length overflows a signed integer, so the
function writes more data than the documented output size. The result is a
heap buffer overflow in the calling process.

Reaching this requires an application to pass an input length near INT_MAX to
EVP_EncodeBlock(). OpenSSL's TLS, QUIC and CMS implementations never encode
buffers of that size, and the command line tools cannot practically be made to
do so: the limits on reading a proxy password from a file and on bignum sizes
prevent it. An application that accepts an attacker-controlled length and
forwards it to EVP_EncodeBlock() without its own bound check is exposed.

The severity is Low because no attacker-controlled path to the overflow is
known. The caller must already hold a buffer of about two gigabytes before the
defect can be reached.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

The Postie plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'email HTML body' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.9.91 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable when the processing request runs under a user holding the unfiltered_html capability — either because 'Force User Login' is enabled and Postie switches to the default poster, or because an administrator manually triggers the fetch — causing wp_filter_post_kses to be stripped from content_save_pre and the attribute-breakout markup to be stored verbatim by wp_insert_post().

The Co-Authors, Multiple Authors and Guest Authors in an Author Box with PublishPress Authors plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'nickname' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.20.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is possible because sanitize_text_field() passes entity-encoded sequences such as < and > through unchanged, allowing a Subscriber to store a breakout payload in their WordPress nickname that is later decoded into live HTML markup by wp_localize_script() and injected into the DOM via jQuery's replaceWith().

The Ultra Addons for Contact Form 7 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'dfile (any CF7 file field)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.5.58 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful script execution additionally requires a web server that returns no explicit Content-Type header for the targeted audio/video extension, causing the browser to sniff and render the uploaded file as text/html; default Apache configurations without mod_headers or without honoring .htaccess satisfy this condition. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The User Registration & Membership – Free & Paid Memberships, Subscriptions, Content Restriction, User Profile, Custom User Registration & Login Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'user_registration_<checkbox_field_name>[]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.3.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The self-registration endpoint (wp_ajax_nopriv_user_registration_user_form_submit) requires no nonce, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to create a Subscriber account and then supply the malicious checkbox value through the authenticated profile-update action using a legitimately obtained nonce.

A flaw was found in OpenSCAP. A heap-based buffer overflow can occur when processing a specially crafted Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF) document using the sds-compose option. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to corrupt memory, resulting in an application crash and a Denial of Service (DoS).
Missing Authorization vulnerability in Drupal S3 File System CORS Upload allows Forceful Browsing. This issue affects S3 File System CORS Upload versions: from 0.0.0 to 1.3.0.

Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Drupal Simple OAuth (OAuth2) & OpenID Connect allows Forceful Browsing. This issue affects Simple OAuth (OAuth2) & OpenID Connect versions: from 0.0.0 to 5.2.6, from 6.0.0 to 6.0.10, from 6.1.0 to 6.1.4.

The MoreConvert Wishlist for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'empty_icon' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This vulnerability is exploitable even in version 2.0.4 where a patch was attempted, because the sanitizer's single html_entity_decode pass combined with esc_attr()'s double_encode=false behavior leaves entity-encoded inner markup intact, which the counter JavaScript then decodes and assigns to innerHTML, turning inert encoded text back into executable DOM elements.
Missing Authorization vulnerability in Drupal Workflow Notifications allows Forceful Browsing. This issue affects Workflow Notifications versions: from 0.0.0 to 3.0.3.

Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel vulnerability in Drupal REST & JSON API Authentication for Drupal allows Authentication Bypass. This issue affects REST & JSON API Authentication for Drupal versions: from 0.0.0 to 3.2.1.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ("Cross-site Scripting") vulnerability in Drupal Highlight Js syntax highlighter allows Reflected XSS. This issue affects Highlight Js syntax highlighter versions: from 0.0.0 to 1.3.1.

Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature vulnerability in Drupal AlternativeCommerce PayPal Checkout allows Signature Spoof. This issue affects AlternativeCommerce PayPal Checkout versions: from 0.0.0 to 1.1.1.
Missing Authorization vulnerability in Drupal Commerce Product Alternative allows Forceful Browsing. This issue affects Commerce Product Alternative versions: from 0.0.0 to 1.0.1.
Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature vulnerability in Drupal Commerce Escrow allows Signature Spoof. This issue affects Commerce Escrow versions: from 0.0.0 to 1.1.0.
Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Drupal Forum Access allows Forceful Browsing. This issue affects Forum Access versions: from 0.0.0 to 2.0.3.
Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ("Cross-site Scripting") vulnerability in Drupal Name Field allows Stored XSS. This issue affects Name Field versions: from 0.0.0 to 1.6.0.
Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Drupal Reset Password Email/SMS OTP allows Forceful Browsing. This issue affects Reset Password Email/SMS OTP versions: from 0.0.0 to 1.0.5.

Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Drupal Scheduler allows Forceful Browsing. This issue affects Scheduler versions: from 0.0.0 to 1.7.0, from 2.2.0 to 2.2.3, from 0.0.0 to 2.0.*, from 0.0.0 to 2.1.*, from 2.3.0 to 2.3.1.
Unverified Password Change vulnerability in Drupal Password Separate Form allows Functionality Bypass. This issue affects Password Separate Form versions: from 0.0.0 to 2.0.3.
Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Drupal Allowed Languages allows Forceful Browsing. This issue affects Allowed Languages versions: from 0.0.0 to 2.0.3.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ("Cross-site Scripting") vulnerability in Drupal Extended HTML Filter allows Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). This issue affects Extended HTML Filter versions: from 0.0.0 to 1.0.4.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ("Cross-site Scripting") vulnerability in Drupal htmLawed allows Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). This issue affects htmLawed versions: from 4.1.0 to 4.1.11.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ("Cross-site Scripting") vulnerability in Drupal htmLawed allows Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). This issue affects htmLawed versions: from 3.0.0 to 3.9.0, from 4.0.0 to 4.1.8.
Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Drupal Islandora  allows Forceful Browsing. This issue affects Islandora  versions: from 0.0.0 to 2.19.1.
Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data vulnerability in Drupal Mime Mail allows Forceful Browsing. This issue affects Mime Mail versions: from 0.0.0 to 2.0.4.
Privilege Defined With Unsafe Actions vulnerability in Drupal AdobeAnalytics allows Stored XSS. This issue affects AdobeAnalytics versions: from 0.0.0 to 1.1.0.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability in Drupal WordsOnline Connector allows SQL Injection. This issue affects WordsOnline Connector versions: from 2.0.0 to 2.0.6.

Strong::Random versions through 0.96 for Perl allow every later rand output to be predicted from three earlier ones.

The generator keeps its state in a single number. Each call multiplies the state by a factor derived from it, and the returned digits encode that factor, so three consecutive outputs determine the state however the generator was seeded. Outputs are also biased: the first digit after the decimal point is never zero, so rand(256) never returns 1 to 24.

An attacker who sees three consecutive outputs can predict the tokens, passwords or key bytes that the same object later issues to other users.

Cross Site Scripting (XSS) in 2.10 Legacy Theming in Apache JSPWIKI version 2.10.0 through 3.0.0 on all platforms allows specially crafted filenames of uploaded attachments to potentially render unescaped html or javascript to the browser.




Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue.

The SlimStat Analytics – Real-Time Stats, Heatmaps & Ecommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HTTP_USER_AGENT' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.1.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the non-default 'Show user agent' (slimstat_options[show_complete_user_agent_tooltip]) setting to be enabled, which causes the raw stored User-Agent value to be used as the tooltip title instead of a sanitized browser name.

Kestra is an open-source control plane for workflows across data, infrastructure, and applications. Prior to version 2.0.1, the namespace-files export endpoint places an unvalidated namespace path segment into the Content-Disposition filename of the ZIP download. An attacker who tricks a user into following a crafted export URL can inject Content-Disposition header parameters to spoof the saved filename or extension. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.1.

The wpForo Forum plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'member[about]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.2.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the attacking subscriber to have met the default antispam threshold of at least 3 forum posts before the account editing page becomes accessible.

The Beautiful taxonomy filters plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'term_name (reflected from DB)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.6.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires an attacker to first create a maliciously-named taxonomy term as an Author-level user; the nonce required to trigger execution is publicly emitted on any front-end page displaying the taxonomy filter widget, making the injected payload reachable by completely unauthenticated visitors.

The plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'custom_text (shortcode attribute of [vc_cta])' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The style="classic" shortcode attribute must be used to trigger the vulnerable code path that feeds custom_text through vc_get_css_color into the inline style attribute; wp_kses_post applied at save time does not neutralize the payload because the attacker's value contains no HTML tags, only a double quote inside a shortcode attribute, leaving the injected content intact in post_content.

An improper access control vulnerability exists in a privileged Unix domain socket of StellarProtect Linux and Stellar Agent (Linux). Due to insufficient authorization checks, a low-privileged local attacker can interact with the daemon and invoke privileged operations without the necessary permissions. This issue affects StellarProtect Linux: 1.0 and earlier; Stellar Agent (Linux): before 1.2.54. *Note: Stellar Agent (Linux) is the new name for StellarProtect Linux.

An authenticated remote code execution vulnerability exists in the firmware update functionality of StellarOne. An attacker with admin privileges can upload a crafted firmware package to execute arbitrary programs with root privileges on the system. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An HTML injection vulnerability exists in the alert notification functionality of StellarOne due to improper sanitization of agent-supplied data. An attacker controlling an agent identity can submit crafted HTML content, potentially allowing the attacker to manipulate displayed content or deceive recipients. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An authenticated remote code execution vulnerability exists in the update functionality of StellarOne due to insufficient validation of files contained within uploaded update packages. An attacker with web administrator privileges can upload a crafted update package to execute arbitrary programs with root privileges on the server. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

A SQL injection vulnerability exists in an Accounts Manager service of StellarOne running inside a container due to improper handling of user-supplied input in SQL queries. An attacker with command execution access to the host system or another container with network connectivity to the affected service can send crafted requests to manipulate backend database queries. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An improper version validation vulnerability exists in the product update mechanism of StellarProtect Linux and Stellar Agent (Linux). An attacker with product admin privileges can downgrade the product to an older, potentially vulnerable version, potentially allowing previously patched vulnerabilities to be reintroduced and security protections to be weakened. This issue affects StellarProtect Linux: 1.0 and earlier; Stellar Agent (Linux): before 1.2.54. *Note: Stellar Agent (Linux) is the new name for StellarProtect Linux.

A remote code execution vulnerability exists in the patch apply functionality of StellarProtect Linux and Stellar Agent (Linux) due to insufficient validation of uploaded patch packages before extraction. An attacker with low-privileged web access can upload a crafted patch package to execute arbitrary programs with root privileges on the server. This issue affects StellarProtect Linux: 1.0 and earlier; Stellar Agent (Linux): before 1.2.54. *Note: Stellar Agent (Linux) is the new name for StellarProtect Linux.

An OS command injection vulnerability exists in the vShell command-line interface of StellarOne due to improper validation of user-supplied input. An authenticated attacker with access to vShell can inject crafted commands to bypass the restricted shell environment and execute arbitrary operating system commands. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An arbitrary file write vulnerability exists in the patch upload functionality of StellarOne due to improper validation of file paths. An attacker with admin web access can upload a crafted patch package to write arbitrary files on endpoints with the privileges of the endpoint service. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

An improper authorization vulnerability exists in the patch management functionality of StellarOne. An attacker with Viewer web access can perform administrative patch management operations. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

A SQL injection vulnerability exists in the Search Agents API of StellarOne due to improper sanitization of user-supplied input. An authenticated attacker with Viewer privileges can send crafted requests to manipulate backend SQL queries. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

The Easy Social Share Buttons for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'position' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 11.6.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload is stored via the unauthenticated wp_ajax_nopriv_ ESSB stat log AJAX action, which performs no nonce or capability check, and executes when the attacker-controlled position value is rendered verbatim into a double-quoted HTML data-* attribute where the unescaped quote allows attribute breakout.

In authd before 0.7.2, an improper access control vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker to complete a first-time SSH login with another account's UID and incorrect primary GID, and to read or modify files owned by that account. This allows an attacker to access another account's data, potentially enabling account takeover or privilege escalation.

The User Frontend – Membership, User Registration, User Profile, User Directory & Content Restriction with Frontend Post Submission plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'post_title' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.14 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that an administrator has configured a wpuf Post Form with guest post submission enabled and placed its shortcode on a public page, from which an unauthenticated attacker can scrape the required nonce before submitting the malicious payload.

The Ninja Tables – Responsive Table Builder for Data, Pricing & Product Tables plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to SQL Injection via the 'dateFormat' column metadata parameter in versions up to, and including, 5.5.1 This is due to insufficient escaping on the stored 'dateFormat' value in DefaultProvider::orderByJsonQuery(); convertDateFormatToMysql() only performs str_replace on date-format tokens and leaves SQL metacharacters (including single quotes) intact, after which the value is concatenated directly into an orderByRaw() ORDER BY clause inside single quotes. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database; the payload is stored in the _ninja_table_columns post meta and executed on every unauthenticated request to the wp_ajax_ninja_tables_public_action AJAX endpoint when the table uses sorting_type='by_column' with a date column.

The WP Data Access – App Builder for Tables, Forms, Dashboards, Charts & Maps plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HyperlinkObject.label (percent-encoded)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.5.92 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the WordPress site to have a published Anonymous-access Registration Form app configured against a table with a HyperlinkObject column, and a legacy Data Project list using a $$link$$ Dynamic Hyperlink against that same column; given this configuration, any unauthenticated visitor can plant the payload.

The Orphans plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.4.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires a two-step comment chain: a benign first comment must be approved under a given name and email so that WordPress's comment_previously_approved mechanism auto-publishes the attacker's payload comment without moderation.

A flaw was found in Foreman. The Red Hat Satellite /unattended/provision API endpoint is vulnerable to an authentication bypass due to a semantic logic flaw in host_verifier.rb. The application verifies the database state of a provisioning token rather than its actual presence in the incoming HTTP request. Because a host actively undergoing provisioning has an unexpired token in the database, the server's valid_host_token? method evaluates to true, granting access to the kickstart template even if the requester provides no token at all in the URL.
Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Arraytics WP Event Solution wp-event-solution allows Object Injection.This issue affects WP Event Solution: from n/a through 4.1.30.

Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in 'activity[description]' field in the POST request to '/people/{person_id}/cvs/{cv_id}/activities' on the job portal. The server stores the data entered by an authenticated candidate and displays it in the recruitment interface without sanitizing it. When reviewing an application, the recruiter’s browser can execute the injected JavaScript code within the context of their session on the portal.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 inserts message-derived values into LDAP filters used by the ldap_compare and ldap_read mail-rule operations without LDAP filter escaping. An unauthenticated remote sender can alter an LDAP-backed rule query when a deployed rule uses attacker-controlled message data, potentially changing policy decisions or exposing data returned to later rule processing.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 copies an insufficiently sanitized DKIM identity into authentication results and may preserve the injected result in an ARC seal. An unauthenticated remote sender can create misleading authentication claims that downstream systems may trust when DKIM verification and ARC sealing are enabled.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 exposes an unauthenticated, world-writable local configuration socket whose root daemon accepts shell commands. An attacker with local low-privilege code execution can execute arbitrary commands as root and take complete control of the appliance.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 interpolates a stored GINA account address into a root boot-job shell command without neutralization. An authenticated internal attacker who can prepare the required account state, arrange for the migration marker to be absent, and cause a reboot can execute arbitrary commands as root.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 reuses a broad legacy GINA session purpose across registration and recovery workflows. A remote attacker who knows an account security answer can use a recovery session in a different account workflow to replace credentials and account recovery data, and may delete the account when self-deletion is enabled.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 permits LDAP wildcard characters in legacy GINA identifiers and inserts those values into account, token, certificate, and key lookup filters without escaping. An unauthenticated remote attacker can alter which directory entry is selected and may disclose account existence or cause later workflow logic to use an unintended entry.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 exposes legacy GINA password-reset paths that can replace a registered account credential without authenticating the requester. A remote attacker who knows the account address can force a reset when a configured administrator or valid stored creator is present, disrupting access and revoking active API tokens; the replacement credential is sent only to a pre-existing trusted recipient.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 uses a source-visible hard-coded fallback secret for legacy GINA token and Large File Transfer cryptographic operations when expected key material is unavailable or unusable. A remote attacker can forge accepted account tokens while the fallback path is active and can decrypt LFT content protected with the shared fallback.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 writes legacy GINA multipart uploads before authenticating the caller and does not remove files created by failed or unauthenticated requests. An unauthenticated remote attacker can accumulate persistent upload files and exhaust the backing filesystem, disrupting GINA and other services sharing that storage.

SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway before 15.1.2 normalizes hyphenated and underscore forms of a trusted GINA routing header to the same backend variable. A remote attacker can create a merged invalid selector that makes legacy GINA and GINAv2 fall back to the default domain policy, potentially crossing tenant or policy boundaries in multi-domain deployments.

The NextMove Lite – Thank You Page for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'billing_address.email' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.24.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected script fires without any victim interaction because the builder page's JavaScript calls $(".preview_order_id").trigger("change") on page load, immediately executing any attribute-injected event handler.

The Themify Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.8.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'textarea-1' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Execution is not automatic on page load; the injected script runs only when an administrator actively clicks the stored ThickBox link, at which point WordPress ThickBox JS decodes the entity-encoded title attribute and writes it into #TB_ajaxWindowTitle via innerHTML in the administrator's origin. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The WPMR Google Feed Manager for WooCommerce – Sell on Google Merchant Center & Shopping plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'feed (title field inside the JSON-encoded feed array)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.24.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with custom-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. sanitize_text_field() is applied on storage but strips only angle brackets and newlines, leaving single quotes and parentheses intact — the exact characters needed to break out of the onclick JavaScript string context constructed by wppfm_feedListTable() and installed via jQuery .append().

A flaw was found in Foreman. A command injection vulnerability exists in the foreman-rake errors:fetch_log task. The request_id parameter is passed to an underlying system command (typically grep) without adequate shell neutralization. While the task is intended to fetch specific log entries, an attacker with sudo permissions to execute this rake task can inject shell metacharacters (such as ;, ", or |) to break out of the intended command and execute arbitrary code.

A flaw was found in Foreman. OS command injection vulnerabilities exist in the foreman-rake db:dump and db:import_dump tasks. The application fails to properly sanitize user-supplied input in the destination parameter (during backups) and the file parameter (during imports) before passing them to a Ruby system() call for execution. An attacker with permissions to execute foreman-rake (e.g., via a restricted sudo configuration) can append malicious shell commands to the provided file paths.

A flaw was found in Foreman. The foreman-rake initialization logic in /usr/share/foreman/config/settings.rb contains a vulnerable code pattern where configuration data is processed through two distinct executable layers. This creates a multi-stage execution chain that allows for both Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) and insecure deserialization. This vulnerability can lead to remote code execution, total infrastructure compromise and supply chain risk.

Cross Site Scripting (XSS) in ListLocksPlugin in Apache JSPWiki 2.10.2 through 3.0.0 on all platforms allows an attacker to execute javascript in the browser of a visitor of a page that uses the plugin. 




Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue.

Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data vulnerability in iHomefinder, Inc. Optima Express optima-express allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data.This issue affects Optima Express: from n/a through 9.0.1.

The Coupon Creator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'metavalue (with metakeyinput=cctor_expiration)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit is possible because the cctor_coupon post type advertises 'custom-fields' support, enabling WordPress core's Custom Fields metabox for Contributors, and the unregistered cctor_expiration meta key causes sanitize_meta() to be a no-op, allowing raw HTML to be stored verbatim in the database via a single AJAX request.

The Funnelforms Free – Multi Step Form, Contact Form & Lead Funnel Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'document.settings.heading' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with administrator-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable on standard single-site WordPress installs only when the DISALLOW_UNFILTERED_HTML constant is set, the site is a WordPress multisite network (where administrators lack the unfiltered_html capability by default), or an administrator has explicitly granted the funnelforms_edit_forms capability to a lower-privileged role. Exploitation by attackers with administrator-level access and above requires that the site is a WordPress multisite install (site admins automatically lack unfiltered_html). On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with custom-level access and above.

Cross Site Scripting (XSS) in the Markdown renderer of Apache JSPWiki 2.11.0 through 3.0.0 on all platforms, when the Markdown syntax is enabled, allows an attacker who can edit a page to execute javascript in the browser of a visitor of that page. The text and the url of an inline image were written into the attributes of the img element without encoding.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue. A fix was also backported to 2.12.6

The Drag and Drop Multiple File Upload (Pro) - WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'wc-upload-file (array key)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.2 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Exploitation requires that the site administrator has enabled the 'Count no. of pages?' option (drag_n_drop_count_pdf set to 'yes') and that the uploaded filename stored in the cart resolves to a file with a .pdf extension.

The WPForms (Contact Form by WPForms / wpforms-lite) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the Multiple Choice field's 'Other' option value on payment forms in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a privileged user such as an administrator accesses the injected payment entry on the WPForms > Payments details page. The submitted value is stored via sanitize_text_field(), which preserves a space-separated pseudo-tag (e.g. '< i class="wpforms-single-payment-tooltip" data-tooltip-content="<img src=x onerror=...>">x< /i>') because strip_tags() ignores a '<' followed by whitespace; on the admin Payments entry page the value is output through wp_kses() with the 'post' allowlist, which normalizes it into a live <i> element retaining its class and data-* attributes, and the bundled Tooltipster initialization (contentAsHTML + contentCloning) then renders the attribute's HTML, executing the script on page load without any hover.

Akaunting 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the XLSX tax-import workflow. An authenticated Manager can import HTML in a tax name and associate the tax with an item. When an Administrator attempts to disable that tax, Akaunting renders the original stored name in an error notification through Vue v-html, causing attacker-controlled markup to execute within the browser of another authenticated user.
