GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 18.10 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with a fine-grained personal access token to read work items in projects or groups they have access to but that were not granted to the token due to incorrect authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 11.7 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with Maintainer-role permissions to cause denial of service due to missing resource limits in the error tracking integration.

A flaw was found in librelp. When configured to use Transport Layer Security (TLS) with certificate validation and the GnuTLS driver, the library fails to verify the peer certificate chain. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this issue by presenting an invalid or self-signed certificate, allowing them to bypass authentication and act as a trusted log source or collector.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, an authenticated manager with access to two advertisers can associate a conversion tracker owned by one advertiser with a campaign owned by the other. The tracker-campaign page checks access to each object but does not verify that their actual owners match. The resulting association can expose the first advertiser's tracker name and identifier in the second advertiser's restricted conversion report.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the public conversion-variable endpoint does not verify that a caller-supplied conversion belongs to the supplied tracker. An unauthenticated attacker can submit a unique variable for a different tracker's conversion, causing that conversion to be classified as a duplicate and excluded from conversion reports.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the zone-linking page can disclose campaign and banner names and identifiers belonging to another agency. An authenticated manager, or a website user with permission to link banners to zones, can supply another agency's advertiser and campaign identifiers because the selection lists are not restricted to the agency owning the zone.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, an authenticated manager can supply another agency's advertiser or website identifier as a report scope and obtain that entity's name in an XLS report header. Submitted scope identifiers are not checked against the manager's permitted selections. The demonstrated disclosure is limited to entity names.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, an advertiser can put XML syntax in fields of its own video creative. Unescaped MediaFile attributes and CDATA terminators allow the advertiser to inject elements into VAST responses served for a publisher's zone. A crafted TrackingEvents block can suppress the ad server's video playback event records and redirect tracking requests to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, user-controlled entity names in XLS report exports can be interpreted as spreadsheet formulas. A user with permission to rename a zone can place a formula in the zone name, which is then included in another user's Conversion Tracking report. Opening the affected spreadsheet can evaluate the formula and alter displayed report contents.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, unauthenticated request parameters in ad delivery can cause reflected cross-site scripting. A crafted delivery URL places a macro token in the source or target parameter and malicious markup in the referer parameter. Macro replacement after initial input encoding can insert the unescaped markup into generated banner output, causing JavaScript execution in the delivery origin when a visitor follows the URL. An active banner is required.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, deleting an agency, advertiser, or publisher through affected API paths can leave the associated account and user session active because the deletion path does not load the entity's account identifier before cleanup. A user whose entity has been deleted can continue accessing pages of the orphaned account. Access to data belonging to another agency was not demonstrated.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the zone banner-linking page (zone-include.php) does not cast the keys of the includebanner request array to integers. An authenticated manager, or a trafficker with the zone-linking permission, who owns the submitted website and zone can place SQL in an array key, which is concatenated unquoted into the banner-lookup query, resulting in time-based blind SQL injection bounded by the privileges of the application's database account.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, the ct0 request parameter of the delivery scripts is only required to start with http:// or https:// and is prepended unescaped to banner click URLs. An unauthenticated attacker can craft a delivery URL that executes JavaScript in the delivery origin when a visitor follows it. An active banner using the raw {clickurl} macro is required.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct an arbitrary file upload attack due to insufficient file type validation. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to upload arbitrary files to the target system. This is MTLVULN-1861.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to leverage pre-staged malicious content to conduct an XML injection attack due to insufficient parameter validation. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. This is MTLVULN-1862.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker, with knowledge of a specific system-generated random identifier or pre-staged content, to conduct an unauthorized access attack due to improper authentication mechanisms. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to obtain sensitive information. The vulnerability is limited to the affected functionality and does not provide unrestricted access to arbitrary files elsewhere on the system. This is MTLVULN-1863.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct a blind command injection attack due to insufficient parameter sanitization. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. This is MTLVULN-1864.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct an authentication bypass attack due to improper handling of authentication. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to bypass authentication and perform unauthorized actions within the context of the application. This is MTLVULN-1877.

Joomla Extension - chronoengine.com - Unauthenticated arbitrary file upload in ChronoForms extension 8.0.0-8.0.53 - When the Filename Provider option of a file field is used, the file extension check is performed against the original client filename instead of the final stored filename, allowing unauthenticated users to upload files with dangerous extensions. Fixed in 8.0.54.

Joomla Extension - chronoengine.com - Unauthenticated SQL injection in table sorting in ChronoForms extension 8.0.0-8.0.53 - The order_by request parameter used for sorting DB Table and Read Data listings is insufficiently sanitized before being added to the ORDER BY clause, allowing unauthenticated users to inject SQL expressions. Fixed in 8.0.54.

Joomla Extension - chronoengine.com - Unauthenticated stored XSS in DB Table cells in ChronoForms extension 8.0.0-8.0.53 - Values rendered in the cells of the DB Table widget are not escaped, allowing unauthenticated users to store JavaScript through form submissions that is executed when the listing is viewed. Fixed in 8.0.54.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - SQL injection via form IDs in administrative form export in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.5, 6.0.0-6.2.2 - Form IDs passed to the administrative form export were not cast to integers before being added to SQL queries, allowing SQL injection by backend users.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing data export permission check in administrative form export in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.5, 6.0.0-6.2.2 - The administrative form export did not check the data export permission when copying form data, allowing backend users without this permission to export submitted form data.

Joomla Extension - vi-solutions - Missing SQL statement permission check in Maxsubmissions plugin in Visforms extension 1.0.0-5.6.5, 6.0.0-6.2.2 - The SQL statement permission was not enforced when saving, importing or batch copying forms with Maxsubmissions plugin settings, allowing backend users without this permission to store arbitrary SQL statements.

Joomla Extension - joomdonation.com - Unauthenticated SQL injection in event registration in Events Booking < 5.12.0 - The event_id submitted through the public registration form was not cast to an integer before being added to an SQL query for the registration's custom fields, allowing unauthenticated SQL injection.

The Xagio SEO & AEO – AI SEO for Google Rankings & AI Visibility plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.0.54 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to modify the XAGIO_SEO_SEARCH_PREVIEW_ENABLE post meta on arbitrary posts, disabling the plugin's SEO title and meta description output for those posts.

The Xagio SEO & AEO – AI SEO for Google Rankings & AI Visibility plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'metavalue (metakeyinput=XAGIO_SEO_SCRIPTS_HEADER)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.0.54 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The Parsigate plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'trackId (Zibal). Equivalent unauthenticated fields for other gateways (e.g. ZarinPal 'Authority', Sep 'RefNum') are logged the same way.' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the non-default 'ParsiGate Log' option to be enabled in plugin settings, at least one WooCommerce order placed via a Parsigate gateway (e.g. Zibal) that remains in a pending state, and an administrator to subsequently view the Tools > ParsiGate Log page.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection') vulnerability in Wikimedia Foundation MediaWiki. This vulnerability is associated with program files includes/libs/Http/MultiHttpClient.php, includes/libs/Mime/MimeAnalyzer.php. This issue affects MediaWiki: 1.47.

In gdm3 before 51.2, an improper privilege management vulnerability allows an unprivileged local attacker with an active GDM graphical session to execute arbitrary code as root by supplying a malicious environment variable during session reauthentication.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.46 through 0.11.1, AutoPilot does not remove the media files that its block runs write to the executor's disk, leading to exhaustion. A signed-in user who can use AutoPilot can grow the temporary storage used by AutoPilot's tool process by about 1 GiB per chat. Once that filesystem is full, file handling fails for every user served by that executor and for anything else writing to the same disk. No other user's data is read or changed. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.2.

SeaweedFS is a distributed storage system for files and blobs. Prior to version 4.46, the S3 gateway does not evaluate bucket policies on POST Object uploads, which are multipart/form-data POST requests to the bucket. An authenticated S3 identity that a bucket policy restricts, such as to a key prefix or by source IP, can create or overwrite objects it is denied by sending the upload as a POST instead of a PUT. This issue has been fixed in version 4.46.

SeaweedFS is a distributed storage system for files and blobs. Prior to version 4.46, FileStore.ValidatePassword in the SFTP server does not reject zero-length secrets before comparing them, causing an empty login password to match any account configured without one, such as public-key-only or certificate-only users. Because password authentication is enabled by default, a remote attacker who knows a valid username can log in without a key or secret and obtain an SFTP session with that user's home directory and path permissions. This issue is fixed in version 4.46.

Glances is an open-source system cross-platform monitoring tool. In versions prior to 4.5.7, the on-alert action command tokenizer in secure.py treats quote characters as argument boundaries without escaping. A monitored stat value, such as a mount point name, that is quoted in an action command template can contain a quote character that breaks out of its quote boundary and injects additional arguments into the process the action invokes. No shell operator is needed for this attack. This issue has been fixed in version 4.5.7.

OpenEXR is the reference implementation and specification for the EXR image format, widely used in the motion picture industry. From versions 3.4.0 through 3.4.18 and 3.5.0 through 3.5.2, decoding a crafted HT-compressed EXR chunk can cause ht_undo_impl() to write a 4-byte pixel value through a pointer that is not 4-byte aligned. This happens when the channels sum to a bytes-per-scanline stride that is not a multiple of four. This issue is fixed in versions 3.4.19 and 3.5.3.

CodeSafe is an open-source Python library for code encryption, decryption, and safe evaluation using Python's AST module. From versions 0.0.1 through 0.0.4, the safe_eval() function can be bypassed with indirect subscript calls such as builtins'exec', because AST validation blocks only direct calls to dangerous built-ins. An attacker who controls an expression passed to safe_eval() can execute arbitrary Python code with the permissions of the host application. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.5.

XO (Xen Orchestra) is a solution to visualize, manage, backup and delegate your XCP-ng (or XenServer) infrastructure. Prior to 6.9.2 and 6.10.1, REST cookie parsing turns authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D into {}. REST authentication passes that object to the XO token provider without requiring a string. The token collection treats {} as an unfiltered lookup and returns its first token; the provider authenticates as that token's owner if it is unexpired. The authenticated /rest/v0/users/me/authentication_tokens route then returns reusable login token IDs. This vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild. This vulnerability is fixed in 6.9.2 and 6.10.1.

The CubeWP Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.32 This is due to the `cubewp_frontend_role_caps()` function, registered on the `user_has_cap` filter, which excludes REST API requests via a `REST_REQUEST` guard but omits a corresponding `XMLRPC_REQUEST` check, causing it to unconditionally widen capabilities for any Subscriber or Contributor on XML-RPC and admin-ajax.php request paths. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Subscriber-level access and above to escalate their privileges to the full Contributor role capability set — gaining `edit_posts`, `delete_posts`, and `read` — allowing them to create, edit, and delete posts through core XML-RPC methods such as `wp.newPost`. Critically, the capability widening is not scoped to CubeWP's own submission handlers but applies globally to all core capability gates on affected request paths, meaning any Subscriber account can exploit this with a single standard XML-RPC call and no CubeWP-specific interaction. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive every capability defined for the Contributor role.

In Dolibarr before 24.0.3, /api/index.php/eventattendees discloses attendee and project data regardless of the caller's permissions. Only 22.0.0 and later (where api_eventattendees.class.php exists) are affected. A remote authenticated user can obtain column values one character at a time.
Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in lyrathemes Kale kale allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Kale: from n/a through 2.9.
Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in ThemeFusion Fusion Builder fusion-builder allows Object Injection.This issue affects Fusion Builder: from n/a before 3.17.1.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in WPVibes AnyWhere Elementor anywhere-elementor allows Stored XSS.This issue affects AnyWhere Elementor: from n/a through 1.3.0.

A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability reflected in the usuario[nombre] parameter of the actualizar_cuenta function in the functions.php endpoint. The application does not properly sanitise the received content, meaning that an authenticated user can inject JavaScript code which is reflected in the web interface and in the JSON responses. If another user views the affected content, the code may be executed within the context of their browser.

With the unanimous access decision strategy, an access_control rule that lists several roles requires all of them. That's the behavior restored by the fix for CVE-2020-5275. Since Symfony 5.4, the access decision manager asked each voter once about all the attributes of a rule. RoleVoter grants access as soon as the user has one of the roles. So a user who had only one of these roles was granted access:

security:
    access_decision_manager:
        strategy: unanimous
    access_control:
- { path: ^/admin, roles: [ROLE_ADMIN, ROLE_AUDITOR] }

Only attributes decided by the same voter were affected. For example, a role combined with allow_if still required both.

With the unanimous strategy, voters are asked about each attribute separately again, as before Symfony 5.4. Access is denied as soon as one of the attributes is denied.

UrlGenerator puts the values of host placeholders into the generated URL without encoding them. Their default requirement, [^.]++, accepts /, @, #, ?, \, % and :. With the host {tenant}.example.com, the value evil%2Ecom# gives https://evil%2Ecom#.example.com/dashboard, which browsers send to evil.com. This works even when requirements are checked. Unicode full stops like 。 have the same effect, since IDNA maps them to ..

Applications are exposed when untrusted values reach host placeholders, for example when they pass the query string of the request to url(). A route that uses RedirectController::redirectAction() with keepQueryParams: true does the same, when the target route has a host placeholder that the redirecting route doesn't define.

UrlGenerator now rejects host placeholder values that contain a character that is forbidden in a host. These characters are C0 controls, space, #, %, /, :, <, >, ?, @, [, \, ], ^, | and DEL. Unicode full stops are rejected too. This check applies whatever strict_requirements is set to. When strict_requirements is false or null, the generator logs an error and returns an empty string instead of throwing. Host placeholder values can still be an IPv6 literal like [::1], but they can't contain a port anymore.

Since Symfony 7.3, the require_tls option of EsmtpTransport refuses to send a message over a connection that isn't encrypted. It prevents a network attacker from stripping STARTTLS. But after the server's 220 reply to STARTTLS, the transport started the TLS handshake without checking whether more data had already arrived.

An attacker in the middle of the connection could add cleartext replies right after the 220. The transport then read them as if they came from the encrypted session. The attacker could make the transport skip AUTH, or report a message as sent while the server had rejected it.

Connections that use implicit TLS, with smtps:// or port 465, are not affected. Since Symfony 8.1, the Amazon SES SMTP transport enables require_tls by default on ports other than 465 and 2465. So ses+smtp:// DSNs are affected without setting the option.

The transport now refuses to start TLS when the server sends data right after its answer to STARTTLS, and throws a TransportException instead.

DoctrineTokenProvider keeps a copy of the previous token of a remember-me cookie. This way, concurrent requests sent with that token are still accepted for 60 seconds. The copy is stored in another row, under a series derived from the series of the cookie. Since Symfony 6.4.45, 7.4.18 and 8.1.6, a copy is stored for every series that the remember-me handler generates. Before, copies were stored only for the series created before Symfony 5.4.19, 6.0.19, 6.1.11 and 6.2.5.

A cookie could use the series of the copy instead of its own series. The copy then matched as a current token, so the limit of 60 seconds didn't apply and the theft detection didn't trigger. Logging out deleted only the row of the original series, and the copy stayed.

An attacker who got hold of a remember-me cookie could then keep logging in as its user after the user logged out. This works when the token was rotated at most once since the attacker got the cookie.

DoctrineTokenProvider now accepts only the series formats that the remember-me handler generates, whatever the collation of the database. It also deletes the copy together with its token.

The fix for CVE-2026-109449 made the expression parser check the nesting level of long expressions. This check exists since Symfony 5.4.54, 6.4.48, 7.4.21 and 8.1.9. The parser builds a ?: b with the node of a used twice, and the check walked every path to every node. With nested short ternaries, the number of paths doubles at each level, so an expression of 256 bytes never finished parsing.

The expression needs no variable and no function. Any code that parses or lints untrusted expressions is affected, including the ExpressionSyntax validation constraint. evaluate() and compile() parse the expression first, so they hang too.

The nesting check now skips the nodes it already checked, so it takes linear time again. evaluate(), compile() and the messages of runtime errors now use the node of a once, so a is evaluated once, as in PHP.

CsvEncoder::decode() splits each header cell on the key separator, . by default, and nests the decoded rows one level per separator, with no limit. PHP frees nested arrays recursively, so freeing data that is nested deeply enough overflows the C stack and crashes the process. With a stack of 8 MB, a CSV body of 448 KB is enough.

Each row also builds all the levels of its headers again. With a deep header, a CSV body of 2 KB made of short rows allocates more than 128 MB. A body of 1 MB keeps the CPU busy for 10 seconds or more.

Any code that decodes untrusted CSV with the Serializer is affected. From Symfony 7.4.0, this included every #[MapRequestPayload] argument that doesn't restrict acceptFormat, until 7.4.23 and 8.1.11 stopped decoding CSV payloads by default.

CSV headers can now be nested up to 512 levels, the default depth of json_decode(). Decoding also stops when the rows go through more than 16 header levels, or create more than 4 arrays, per byte of data. A header row of up to 5 levels always fits, whatever the rows contain. Beyond these limits, decode() throws a NotEncodableValueException, which #[MapRequestPayload] turns into a 400 response.

Since Symfony 7.4.0, FrameworkBundle chooses the error renderer from the runtime mode of the application, which comes from the APP_RUNTIME_MODE env var. When this variable isn't set, the cli, phpdbg and embed SAPIs default to the CLI mode, and errors are rendered with CliErrorRenderer. This renderer dumps the whole exception, and it did so even when debug was off.

HTTP workers that run under the CLI SAPI and don't set APP_RUNTIME_MODE then sent these dumps as error responses in production. They contain the messages, file paths and traces of the exceptions. Some exceptions reference the request, like the access denied errors of access_control rules. Their dump then contains the server parameters, with all the environment variables of the application.

This affects, for example, the RoadRunner, Swoole and ReactPHP runners of php-runtime, and baldinof/roadrunner-bundle before 3.2.4. The worker mode of FrankenPHP sets the variable and isn't affected.

The CLI renderer is now used only in debug mode.

The controllers.json loader of @symfony/stimulus-bridge loads the package.json file of each package listed in controllers.json with require(). Node resolves this path through the exports field of the package, which can map ./package.json to a script. require() then runs that script during the Webpack or Symfony Encore build.

This is a build-time vulnerability: it doesn't affect browsers or end users. A malicious or compromised package listed in controllers.json can run code on the developer machine or the CI server. This works even when the package manager doesn't run install scripts. This code can read the files and environment variables of the build, like CI secrets, and change the built assets.

The loader now reads the resolved file and parses it as JSON, so that a mapped script fails to parse instead of running.

A flaw was found in KubeVirt/containerized-data-importer. When a VirtualMachine with an embedded DataVolumeTemplate carrying the cdi.kubevirt.io/storage.checkStaticVolume annotation and a cross-namespace clone source is created by a tenant, the service-account clone authorization check can be bypassed, allowing a PVC from another namespace to be cloned into the tenant's namespace without the required permissions. This can result in cross-tenant data disclosure.

The WPFunnels – Funnel Builder for WooCommerce with Checkout & One Click Upsell plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to sensitive information disclosure in versions up to, and including, 3.13.8 This is due to the wpfnl_register_dashboard_widgets() function  registering the 'WPFunnels Overview' dashboard widget on the wp_dashboard_setup hook with no capability check on either the registration or the wpfnl_dashboard_overview_widget() callback, which queries the wpfnl_stats and wpfnl_optin_entries tables and echoes the store's completed-order count, total revenue, order-bump revenue, upsell/downsell revenue and total lead/optin count directly into the dashboard. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above (contributor-level on sites running WooCommerce, where WC_Admin::prevent_admin_access() blocks subscribers from reaching /wp-admin/index.

The Simple Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in versions up to, and including, 4.8.9 This is due to the site-wide signing secret `swpm_private_key_one` being generated at install time with PHP's non-cryptographic `uniqid('', true)` function in `SwpmInstallation::installer()`, whose timestamp-derived keyspace (~10^15 candidates / ~50 bits) can be constrained via the public WordPress REST API date of the plugin's auto-created registration page, combined with a single-MD5 oracle (`md5(key|level)`) that the public registration form prints as `swpm_level_hash` and a non-constant-time `!=` comparison in `SwpmFrontRegistration::register_front_end()` as the sole authorization gate on which membership level a visitor may register into; `SwpmUtils::get_free_level()` then honors an attacker-posted `level_identifier=md5(level)` regardless of the configured free-membership setting, and `prepare_and_create_wp_user_front_end()` creates the WordPress account with whatever role the level is configured to grant (only the `administrator` role is refused). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers, after an offline brute-force recovery of the install-time secret against the public MD5 oracle, to forge a valid `swpm_level_hash` for any configured membership level and self-register into that level, elevating their newly created WordPress account to the level's assigned role — e. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete editor role.

An authentication bypass vulnerability exists in the web management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to gain unauthorized administrative access to the affected system, impacting the confidentiality and integrity of AirWave.

A vulnerability in system functionality could allow an attacker with network access to bypass authentication. Successful exploitation could potentially allow an attacker to perform unauthorized actions, affecting system integrity and confidentiality.

A command injection vulnerability exists in the web-based management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands on the underlying operating system of the affected system, impacting the confidentiality, integrity and availability of HPE Networking Management Software (AirWave).

A vulnerability in a system functionality could allow a low-privilege authenticated attacker with network access to potentially authenticate as an unintended user. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to gain unauthorized access, potentially affecting system integrity, exposing sensitive information, or disrupting management operations.

Authenticated SQL injection vulnerabilities in the web-based management interface and API of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave) could allow a low-privileged authenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary SQL statements against HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to obtain sensitive information from and modify data on the affected system.

A missing integrity verification vulnerability exists in HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow a low-privileged local attacker to modify trusted system data on the affected system.

A sensitive information disclosure vulnerability exists in the affected interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain sensitive information from the affected system.

A command injection vulnerability exists in the web-based management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an authenticated remote attacker with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands on the underlying operating system if certain preconditions outside of the attacker's control are met.

Improper certificate validation vulnerabilities in the web-based management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave) allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to circumvent existing authentication controls if certain preconditions outside of the attacker's control are met. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to gain administrative access to the affected system.

Path traversal vulnerabilities exist in the web-based management interface and API of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave), which could be exploited by an authenticated attacker with low privileges. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to read certain files on the underlying operating system.

A vulnerability was detected in eigent-ai eigent up to 1.0.2. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file backend/app/controller/chat_controller.py of the component Local Agent Control API. Performing a manipulation results in missing authentication. The attack may be initiated remotely. Upgrading to version 1.0.3 addresses this issue. The patch is named 59f43afcb1b0ba7b2de8c65d585124f196c4aa17. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.
Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in MotoPress Getwid getwid allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Getwid: from n/a through 3.0.3.

A security flaw has been discovered in D-Link DIR-600L 2.17b02. This affects the function FUN_0040efb0 of the file gena.cgi of the component GENA Subscription Handler. Performing a manipulation of the argument service results in stack-based buffer overflow. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks.

Open Robotics ROS 2 sros2 load_policy XML External Entity Processing Information Disclosure Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to disclose sensitive information on affected installations of Open Robotics ROS 2. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of policy XML files. Due to the improper restriction of XML External Entity (XXE) references, a crafted document specifying a URI causes the XML parser to access the URI and embed the contents back into the XML document for further processing. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the current user. Was ZDI-CAN-32121.

The Ultra Addons for Contact Form 7 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthorized access of data due to a missing authorization check on the UACF7_CUSTOM_FIELDS shortcode in versions up to, and including, 3.5.59 The shortcode handler  accepts an attr value of the form 'post_id/meta_key', normalizes the parts with absint() and sanitize_key(), and calls get_post_meta() without verifying that the current user is authorized to read that post (no current_user_can('read_post', $id) or post_status check). This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to read arbitrary post meta, including private/draft post meta and third-party plugin PII (e.

The Premium Packages - Sell Digital Products Securely plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in versions up to, and including, 7.3.4 This is due to the cancel_subscription(), toggleAutoRenew() and toggleManualRenew() AJAX handlers performing no ownership or capability check on the user-supplied `orderid` parameter — the only gate is a plugin-wide NONCE_KEY nonce that is emitted to any visitor on every product page. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to cancel other customers' subscriptions, flip `auto_renew` and toggle the `manual_renew` meta on any order by supplying its ID.

Improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic in the query construction of AWS Graph Explorer before 3.2.1 might allow an authenticated remote user with write access to the connected graph database to access and modify data in that database with Graph Explorer's privileges via a crafted property key or label that is used when another user performs a search.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to Graph Explorer version 3.2.1 or later.

A stack-based buffer overflow in the replication origin name parsing component in AWS pgactive before 2.1.10 might allow an authenticated remote user to execute arbitrary operating system commands as the database operating system user via a crafted replication origin name.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to pgactive version 2.1.10 or later.

Improper input validation in the AWS-managed AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3 might allow an authenticated remote user who is permitted to run the runbook to set unintended configuration in the account's Regional Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) via a crafted S3KeyPrefix parameter value. This applies only when that document does not already exist in the Region. The unintended configuration can include arbitrary commands, which then run on managed instances when other users start Session Manager sessions.



Because any user permitted to run the runbook selects which revision to run, this issue remains reachable in an affected Region until earlier revisions can no longer be run there. AWS is deprecating all revisions created before 2026-10-22 (UTC) in every Region and partition beginning January 15, 2027; until deprecation, earlier revisions remain runnable, so upgrading alone is not sufficient.



To remediate this issue:



1. Run the latest revision of the runbook. The latest revision is the fixed revision in every Region where the runbook is available, and its revision number varies by Region. To find it, run aws ssm describe-document --name AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3 --region <region> --query "Document.LatestVersion". Update any Automation executions, State Manager associations, AWS Config remediation configurations, or other automations pinned to an earlier revision to use the latest revision. 2. Until earlier revisions are removed in your Region, either keep untrusted users from running earlier revisions of the runbook, or keep a trusted Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) in every Region. Earlier revisions inject only when they create this document, so while a trusted one exists, this path is closed in that Region. 3. Review your Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) in any Region where it was first created by an earlier revision of this runbook, not by you. To check, look for any run of this runbook that failed with "DOCUMENT CREATE OR UPDATE FAILED." An injected run always fails with this error. You can also compare the creation date of the document's first version with the start times of runs of this runbook in that Region. Check the document for settings you did not configure, especially shellProfile, Run As (runAsEnabled, runAsDefaultUser), maxSessionDuration, idleSessionTimeout, and the logging destination fields. The fixed runbook updates only the S3 bucket and prefix fields of an existing preferences document, so settings injected earlier remain until you remove them. If you find unexpected settings, restore your trusted preferences and review instances on which Session Manager sessions were started while those settings were active. The AWS Security Bulletin includes commands for this review.

The WordPress File Upload plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion in versions up to, and including, 5.3.1 via the 'wfu_ajax_action_handshake' and 'wfu_ajax_action_send_email_notification' AJAX Actions. This is due to the unauthenticated handshake accepting a 'sid' parameter sanitized only with sanitize_text_field(), which does not strip '[', ']', '{', or '}', allowing the sid to be crafted as an item name containing embedded delimiter pairs that plant forged records for arbitrary other item names — including the per-session file path list and the consent flag — in the plugin's shared concatenated user-state option store, combined with the notification handler being gated only by a nonce freely minted by the same nopriv handshake. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the affected site's server which may make remote code execution possible.

The WP Review Slider plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Read in versions up to, and including, 15.5 via the wprp_twitter_savetweet and wpfb_avatar_tolocal AJAX actions. This is due to the handlers only verifying a WordPress nonce without any current_user_can() capability check and accepting an attacker-supplied local filesystem path in the 'tw_img' parameter, which is later passed directly to PHP's copy() to write byte-identical data into a publicly accessible uploads directory under an attacker-chosen name. The nonce action 'randomnoncestring' is shared with the same vendor's companion plugin (WP Google Review Slider), which emits it to every visitor of every front-end page, making it obtainable by any logged-in user including Subscribers whenever that companion plugin is active. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to read arbitrary files on the affected site's server, including sensitive files such as wp-config.

SiYuan 3.6.0 before 3.6.2 and 3.7.3 before 3.8.10 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the /api/block/getDOMText endpoint, which renders caller-supplied DOM without checking publish access for referenced image paths. When publish authentication is disabled, anonymous visitors can submit DOM referencing a known unpublished, non-encrypted asset path to retrieve its already-cached OCR text.

Grav Form plugin 1.1.0 before 9.1.40 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in Form::uploadFiles(), which sanitizes SVG only when a file's last extension is .svg and accepts markup under unrecognized extensions. Anonymous attackers can upload files like drawing.svg.foo through public any-type upload forms, running script in an administrator's session when opened, enabling super-admin creation on Grav 2.x with Admin2.

Admidio from 5.0.17 before 5.0.18 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated regular users to upload images into the announcements module by abusing the CKEditor upload handler. Attackers can send id=ann_description to ckeditor_upload_handler.php to store images under adm_my_files/announcements/images and retrieve them via show_image.php, abusing the application as an image host.

Admidio 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in modules/profile/profile_new.php that allows authenticated Group Leaders to bypass field-level profile restrictions. Attackers can request mode=html_selection to read restricted field values and submit mode=save requests to modify restricted member profile fields.

Vikunja from 0.19.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated users to exhaust CPU by supplying unbounded business-day operands in datemath filters. Attackers can send task or time-tracking filters like due_date > now+999999999999b, triggering a per-day loop in go-datemath that pins CPU cores and exhausts the server.

Vikunja from 0.19.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated CalDAV users to exhaust server CPU by uploading VTODO properties with many parameters. Attackers can PUT an iCalendar body with thousands of parameters on one line to any valid project ID, triggering superlinear parsing before permission checks.

Vikunja from 2.2.1 before 2.8.0 contains a TOTP replay protection bypass in ValidateTOTPPasscode that allows attackers to reuse consumed codes by padding them with whitespace. Attackers with valid credentials who observe a used passcode can resubmit it whitespace-padded to the login API within the validity window to obtain a session token.

Vikunja 0.17.0 before 2.8.0 builds the task.deleted notification and webhook payload, including related tasks, with the deleting user's permissions and sends it to all project subscribers without per-recipient authorization checks. A user subscribed to a project, or owning its webhook, receives full data of related tasks in private projects they cannot read when a task in their project is deleted.

OpenRemote core before 1.34.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in UserAssetProvisioningMQTTHandler that allows unauthenticated attackers to impersonate provisioned devices without proof of private key possession. Attackers can publish a known device's public certificate to the provisioning request topic, authenticating their anonymous MQTT connection as the device's service account to read and modify assets.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in its filesystem storage bucket that only canonicalizes the bucket root, not descendant symlinks. Attackers can reference paths through a pre-existing symlink inside the bucket that pass the lexical prefix check, reading and writing files across the host filesystem.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass that allows users with the read-only VIEWER role to modify database schema, because CREATE on a nonexistent table implicitly defines it without the DEFINE TABLE permission check applied to explicit definitions. Authenticated VIEWER users can issue CREATE statements in non-STRICT databases to add arbitrary empty SCHEMALESS tables, cluttering schemas or colliding with application table names.

SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows any user able to run queries to crash the server by triggering unchecked decimal overflow in math::sum or math::product. SurrealDB from 3.2.0 before 3.3.4 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows record users to update protected rows by exploiting table-level PERMISSIONS FOR update predicates referencing COMPUTED fields. better-auth 1.3.7 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains a race condition in the emailOTP plugin attempt counter, collision-prone email change code keys, and accent-insensitive email lookups. ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the Redis protocol handler, which neither replies to nor closes a pre-authentication connection when it receives an array whose first element is not a string. The fix for CVE-2017-16652 restricts the redirects of HttpUtils::createRedirectResponse() to the host of the request. When framework.session.cookie_domain is set, it also allows the subdomains of that domain. To check a target, it read the host of the URL up to the first "/". But browsers also end the host at "\", "?" and "#". So with the cookie domain .example.com, a target like https://evil.test?.example.com passed the check, and the browser went to evil.test.

Applications are exposed when framework.session.cookie_domain is set. The default success and failure handlers of form_login redirect to the _target_path or _failure_path of the request. A login link can then send the user to another site right after a successful login, for example to ask for the password again.

HttpUtils now ends the host of a target where browsers do, before checking it against the allowed domains.

Since Symfony 7.2, expressions can contain comments. The lexer used a regular expression to find the end of a comment. When a /* was never closed, this regular expression scanned the rest of the expression, and the lexer then went on with the next character. So each /* scanned the rest of the expression again. Linting 192 KB of /*  took 9 to 11 seconds, and 96 KB took 34 seconds without PCRE JIT.

The lexer runs before the parser and its nesting limit. Any code that lints or parses untrusted expressions is affected, including the ExpressionSyntax validation constraint. A Length constraint on the same value doesn't help, since the validator runs both constraints.

The lexer now uses strpos() to find the end of a comment, and a comment that is never closed throws a SyntaxError. Such expressions were already invalid. Lexing takes linear time again.

When the proxy option isn't set, HttpClient takes the proxy from environment variables like http_proxy or HTTP_PROXY. On web servers, it ignores HTTP_PROXY, because PHP puts the Proxy request header there (the httpoxy issue). On the CLI SAPI, it read HTTP_PROXY from $_SERVER, where PHP also puts the environment.

HTTP workers that run under the CLI SAPI put the headers of each request in $_SERVER too. This is the case of spiral/roadrunner-http, which the RoadRunner runner of php-runtime uses, and of baldinof/roadrunner-bundle and php-pm. A client could then send a Proxy header to choose the proxy of the requests that the application sent while handling its request. That proxy received the full requests to http:// URLs, with their credentials, and could forge the responses. For https:// URLs, it learned the host and port through CONNECT.

NativeHttpClient is affected since Symfony 4.3.0, AmpHttpClient since 5.1.0, and CurlHttpClient since 4.4.40, 5.4.7 and 6.0.7.

On the CLI SAPI, HTTP_PROXY is now read from the environment with $_ENV and getenv(), never from $_SERVER. Other SAPIs still ignore it.

When a PDF is opened, readxrtr reads each cross-reference table and calls itself on the offset in the trailer's /Prev entry. Nothing records which offsets it has already read, so a /Prev entry pointing back to an earlier table, or to its own, makes it recurse without end.

An attacker who supplies a crafted PDF can cause a denial of service in any application that opens it.
Rejected reason: This CVE has been rejected by Upstream. Ref: https://bugzilla.samba.org/show_bug.cgi?id=16047#c4

An invalid memory release in the MongoDB PHP Driver extension occurs when certain string-typed options or type-mapping settings are given non-string values. A party who can run PHP code in a process that loads the extension may corrupt process memory. This can lead to reading or changing process memory, running commands as the PHP process user, or crashing the process.

Mongoid builds an incomplete automatic encryption schema for certain embedded document associations. As a result, values that the application declared as encrypted may be written to the database in cleartext, with no error or warning returned to the application. A party holding only basic read privileges on the affected collection, and no access to the encryption keys, may then obtain those values in readable form.

Mongoid does not consistently apply its read-only attribute protection when attribute names are supplied dynamically by the caller. In an application that forwards caller-supplied attribute names into a document update, a user with basic application privileges may change values held inside a field the model declared immutable. This may result in unintended modification of data the application treats as trusted, such as flags used for its own access decisions.

Mongoid contains an incorrect authorization weakness in the handling of caller-supplied filters for bulk removal through a referenced association. Conditions already attached to the association can take precedence over the filter the caller supplied, so records the caller did not select may be removed. A user with basic privileges in an application built on the library may cause unintended removal of records belonging to the same parent record.

Mongoid may omit a field from the client-side encryption settings it generates for a collection when that same field is also used as a reference to another record. The value is then stored in readable form instead of encrypted, and the application receives no indication that this has happened. A party with ordinary authenticated read access to the affected collection may be able to view data that was intended to be protected.

A logic flaw in the query-building layer of the Mongoid object-document mapper causes a model-level default restriction that is meant to return no records to be silently discarded when it is combined into a query. A user with basic application privileges who sends an ordinary request may read, change, or remove records that the restriction was intended to withhold.

An incorrect authorization weakness in the embedded relation handling of the Laravel MongoDB library may allow a user with basic application privileges to alter records belonging to other users. After an embedded relation is pre-loaded, a routine write on that record is issued without the constraint that limits it to the record the user is permitted to change. This may result in unintended modification or loss of stored data for other users of the same application.

A query builder component in a MongoDB integration library for a PHP web framework does not run the query-modification callbacks that an application registers with the framework before sending read, update, and delete operations to the database. As a result, a filter that an application relies on to limit which records a request may touch can be omitted silently. A user with basic application privileges may be able to read or change records that the application intended to keep out of reach.

A polymorphic relationship query helper in the MongoDB Eloquent integration for Laravel resolves a record's type identifier inconsistently between the code that stores a relationship link and the code that searches for one. An application that relies on a relationship-absence query to restrict which records a request may see or change can therefore have that restriction silently fail, allowing a user with basic application privileges to read and to modify or remove records the restriction was meant to cover.

An improper certificate revocation check in the MongoDB Python Driver's optional TLS revocation-checking support allows an unauthenticated party that operates the network endpoint a client connects to, and that holds a revoked but still-dated certificate trusted by that client, to have the connection accepted. This may result in unintended disclosure of application credentials and other session data, and in the client treating responses from that endpoint as genuine.

A data-query neutralization weakness in the query builder of the MongoDB integration for a PHP web framework allows values supplied to certain bulk counter-update helpers to be interpreted by the database as query expressions rather than stored as plain text. An application that passes externally supplied data into these helpers may write unintended values into stored documents and may result in unintended disclosure of other data held on the same document. No credentials are required of the party supplying the value.

The Download Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'file[files][]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.78 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that the affected package uses a link template containing the [play_button] shortcode, such as the bundled 'With Audio Preview' template, since the vulnerable audioPlayer() output path is only triggered when that placeholder is rendered.

The Download Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'file[page_template], file[files][]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.78 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The Download Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.78 via the 'file[page_template]' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to include and execute arbitrary .php files on the server, allowing the execution of any PHP code in those files. This can be used to bypass access controls, obtain sensitive data, or achieve code execution in cases where .php file types can be uploaded and included. The malicious page_template value is stored when an Author creates or edits a package post, and the inclusion is triggered on any subsequent page view of the package permalink, meaning the include() can be fired by unauthenticated visitors after the payload is planted.

In Eclipse Ditto versions 0.3.0-M1 through 3.8.15 and 3.9.0 through 3.9.9, the JavaScript payload mapper of the connectivity service executes user-supplied mapping scripts in a Mozilla Rhino engine without a ClassShutter. A mapping script can catch an engine error and use the Java exception object exposed on it to reach arbitrary Java classes and methods via reflection, bypassing the documented sandbox restriction that mapping scripts cannot access Java packages or classes. This allows a user permitted to create or modify connections (by default the Ditto DevOps realm) to execute arbitrary code in the connectivity service, gaining access to its credentials and to the Ditto cluster.

@fastify/middie is the plugin that adds Express-style middleware support to the Fastify web framework. In versions 9.3.6 through 9.3.9, a route or mount path written without a leading slash inside a plugin registered under a prefix is handled inconsistently: the middleware is mounted with a separating slash after the prefix, while the route is concatenated directly onto the prefix, so a request to the concatenated path reaches the route handler without running the middleware mounted for it. An attacker can use this to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on the affected routes. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.10, and users should upgrade to 9.3.10 or later. As a workaround, begin all route and mount paths with a slash, or enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router resolves the request.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 18.10 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to perform server-side request forgery against internal network resources due to insufficient URL validation in MCP server OAuth handling.

An improper handling of repeated fields in encryption key documents in the MongoDB encryption support library may allow memory to be retained without release. A party able to write to the key storage collection, or a database endpoint returning such a document, may cause the memory use of the calling application process to grow for each document parsed, which may reduce performance of that process.

An information exposure weakness in the connection string handling of the MongoDB Ruby Driver can place credential material from the application's own configuration into the text of a parsing error, where an existing redaction control does not apply. A party able to read the application's error output or logs may thereby obtain database credential text together with deployment coordinates. The condition arises entirely within the embedding application process and requires no database authentication.

A type-confusion weakness in the Extended JSON parsing component of BSON for Ruby allows a party who can supply parser input to influence how a serialized document is framed. Content placed in one value may be read back as additional or replacement document fields. An unauthenticated party supplying input to an application that parses untrusted Extended JSON and stores the result may cause unintended modification of stored data.

An improper restriction of dynamically determined object attributes in the object-document mapping library's association handling allows structured input supplied in place of a simple identifier value to be turned into an object that is treated as an already-stored record of a caller-chosen model class. In applications that pass unfiltered request data into the affected association handling, an unauthenticated party may cause unintended modification or removal of stored records, and may render an individual record unreadable through that association.

A vulnerability in the MongoDB integration package for the Laravel framework allows an unauthorized user to bypass mass assignment attribute protections. When an application uses attribute deny-lists to guard sensitive model fields, specially crafted request payloads containing database operator keys can circumvent these protections. An unauthorized user with network access to an affected application endpoint can modify guarded attributes, potentially leading to privilege escalation within the application

@fastify/express is the plugin that lets an application run Express middleware and Express applications inside the Fastify web framework. In versions from 4.0.3 before 4.0.14, the plugin decodes certain percent-encoded characters in the request path that Express would otherwise keep encoded, including the Unicode line separator and paragraph separator characters, and leaves them raw. A JavaScript regular expression treats those two characters as line terminators, so a regular-expression mount path that relies on the dot metacharacter fails to match a request containing them while Fastify's own router still routes the request to its handler, and the middleware mounted on that regular-expression path is therefore skipped. An attacker can use this to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on routes guarded by a regular-expression mount; string mount paths are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.14, and users should upgrade to 4.0.14 or later. As a workaround, use string mount paths, avoid the dot metacharacter in regular-expression mounts by using a character class or the dotAll flag, or enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router resolves the request.

@fastify/express is the plugin that lets an application run Express middleware and Express applications inside the Fastify web framework. In versions from 4.0.7 before 4.0.14, when middleware is mounted on a nested array of mount paths the plugin rewrites only the top level of the array, so paths inside a nested array are not adjusted for a plugin registered under a prefix and the middleware never runs for them, a nested regular-expression mount keeps its global or sticky flag and is matched statefully so it is skipped on alternating requests, a nested regular expression is not matched case-insensitively when case sensitivity is disabled, and nested dynamic paths are not covered by the earlier empty-segment check. An attacker can use any of these to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on the affected routes. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.14, and users should upgrade to 4.0.14 or later. As a workaround, flatten mount path arrays before passing them to the plugin, or enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router resolves the request.

The Music Player for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 1.9.4 via the '_downloadable_files' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. Staging the attack requires storing a crafted downloadable file URL against a product, which requires the edit_products capability (Shop Manager or above); however, triggering the file read via the ?wcmp-action=play handler is fully unauthenticated once the crafted URL is saved to a published product.

The Relevanssi – A Better Search plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'name (REST /wp/v2/tags) / tax_input[post_tag] (post save)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.28.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable because WordPress's wp_filter_kses stores entity-encoded payloads (e.g., <img src=x onerror=...>) verbatim as literal text in the database, but Relevanssi's relevanssi_entity_decode() subsequently converts them into live HTML markup before the unescaped return branch of relevanssi_the_tags() splices them into the tag list consumed by the theme.

The WPC Linked Variation for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'wpclv_link[source]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.6.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The wpclv custom post type is accessible to Contributor-level users, meaning a Contributor can craft a malicious Linked Variation post whose payload fires in the session of any higher-privileged user (e.g., Administrator or Editor) who opens the post edit screen to review it.

@fastify/express is the plugin that lets an application run Express middleware and Express applications inside the Fastify web framework. In versions from 4.0.5 before 4.0.14, a mount path that begins with an Express 5 optional leading segment written as a group is treated as relative and has a slash prepended when it is joined to the plugin prefix, which changes what the pattern matches so the middleware ends up mounted on a path that no longer corresponds to the real request paths. The middleware therefore never runs for requests that match the intended routes, while the Fastify routes still resolve to their handlers. An attacker can use this to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on the affected routes. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.14, and users should upgrade to 4.0.14 or later. As a workaround, mount the middleware on each path spelling explicitly, or enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after the router resolves the request.

@fastify/express is the plugin that lets an application run Express middleware and Express applications inside the Fastify web framework. In versions before 4.0.14, a request with an empty dynamic route parameter reaches a Fastify route handler while middleware mounted for that path inside an Express Router or sub-application is skipped, because Fastify's router accepts an empty value where Express requires a non-empty one, and an unanchored regular-expression mount passed to the plugin is bypassed the same way. An earlier fix covered only the mount paths passed to the plugin directly, not middleware mounted inside a routed Express application. An attacker can use this to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on the affected routes, with the practical impact depending on what the empty value selects in the application. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.14, and users should upgrade to 4.0.14 or later. As a workaround, enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, mount the middleware on a static parent path, or require non-empty values in the route params schema.

@fastify/express is the plugin that lets an application run Express middleware and Express applications inside the Fastify web framework. In versions before 4.0.14, when an application enables case-insensitive routing, middleware mounted on a path can still be skipped in two cases: a string mount path or plugin prefix containing a Unicode character whose case folding differs from a plain lowercase conversion fails to match the lowercased request path, and a matcher that stays case-sensitive inside an Express Router or application, such as a regular expression without the ignore-case flag or an explicitly case-sensitive router, only matches its own casing. In both cases a request reaches the Fastify route handler while the path-scoped middleware does not run. An attacker can use this to bypass authentication or other middleware-based access controls on the affected routes, and only applications that enable case-insensitive routing are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.14, and users should upgrade to 4.0.14 or later. As a workaround, enforce authentication in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, avoid such Unicode characters in mount paths, and match case-insensitively inside Express routers and applications.

Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.42.10, RoleGuard authorizes requests using the role claim embedded in an access token instead of the user's current database role in packages/core/src/lib/core/context/request-context.ts through RequestContext.hasRoles. After an administrator demotes a user, an already-issued token can continue to pass role checks for up to the token's 24-hour default lifetime, including on DELETE /api/tenant and other RolesEnum.SUPER_ADMIN or ADMIN guarded routes, which can preserve tenant-destructive and billing privileges after revocation. This issue is fixed in version 111.42.10.

Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.44.3, per-request JWT validation in packages/core/src/lib/auth/strategies/jwt.strategy.ts accepts the result of UserService.getIfExists in packages/core/src/lib/user/user.service.ts without requiring User.isActive to be true and User.isArchived to be false. When a token contains an organizationId claim, the active and archived status check applies to the UserOrganization record rather than the User entity. After an administrator deactivates an account through PATCH /api/user/:id, an existing access token can continue to authenticate API requests at the account's previous privilege level until expiration, up to 24 hours by default. This issue is fixed in version 111.44.3.

Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.42.9, OrganizationPermissionGuard in packages/core/src/lib/shared/guards/organization-permission.guard.ts checks allowManualTime, allowModifyTime, and allowDeleteTime only when the caller's role is EMPLOYEE and unconditionally authorizes other roles. A tenant administrator who grants ALLOW_MANUAL_TIME, ALLOW_MODIFY_TIME, or ALLOW_DELETE_TIME to MANAGER, DATA_ENTRY, VIEWER, or another non-employee role can therefore leave the organization-wide policy disabled while that role still creates, modifies, or deletes time records, undermining payroll and billing integrity. This issue is fixed in version 111.42.9.

Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.42.13, POST /api/integration/github/webhook in packages/plugins/integration-github/src/lib/probot/probot.discovery.ts passes request bodies through ProbotDiscovery.receiveHook to probot.receive without verifying x-hub-signature-256 against the configured webhook secret. Because the route is public and uses the attacker-controlled installation.id to locate integrations, an unauthenticated remote attacker who knows or guesses an installation identifier can forge installation deletion events that remove a tenant's GitHub integration or forge issues events that insert fabricated issue data into the tenant's automation pipeline. This issue is fixed in version 111.42.13.

Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.44.2, getTracker in packages/core/src/lib/throttler/throttler-behind-proxy.guard.ts accepts CF-Connecting-IP without verifying that a trusted Cloudflare edge supplied it; when CF-Connecting-IP is absent, app.set('trust proxy', true) can let an attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-For value determine req.ip. In deployments where a trusted intermediary does not overwrite these headers, or where the firewall permits direct API access, varying the applicable header on repeated POST /auth/login requests gives an unauthenticated remote attacker a distinct throttle bucket for each attempt, so the five-attempts-per-60-seconds limit does not trigger and no account lockout, CAPTCHA, or exponential backoff limits password guessing. This issue is fixed in version 111.44.2.

Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.42.11, singleton-scoped ExportService stores the per-request identifiers this.idCsv and this.idZip as BehaviorSubjects and keeps derived directory names in instance fields, while singleton-scoped ImportService stores per-request paths in this._dirname and this._extractPath. Concurrent requests by different tenant administrators to /export, /export/template, /export/filter, or /import can interleave while asynchronous file operations are in progress, allowing one tenant's export archive to be delivered, overwritten, or deleted by another operation, or causing one tenant's import to read another tenant's uploaded CSV data and persist it under the wrong tenant. This issue is fixed in version 111.42.11.

Server-side request forgery in Amazon OpenSearch Service service software before R20260720 might allow an authenticated user with permission to manage snapshots to make the service send requests to network destinations of their choosing via the snapshot repository endpoint setting. This issue is addressed in service software R20260720. Customers should update their domains to R20260720 or later.

Munshi (by Petpooja) before 2026-07-07 contained a broken object level authorization vulnerability in the PUT /api/invoice/{invoice_id}/extracted-data endpoint, which accepts a client-supplied extracted_data object without verifying invoice ownership, enforcing the invoice_edit permission or checking whether the invoice has been soft deleted. Authenticated attackers who know an invoice identifier can overwrite seller and buyer details, invoice identifiers, product entries, totals and custom metadata of invoices, including archived invoices marked is_deleted = 1, undermining the integrity of financial records.

Munshi (by Petpooja) before 2026-07-15 contained a stored HTML injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to store markup in the profile full_name field by submitting a modified request directly to the backend, which persists the value without sanitization. The Contact Support workflow later inserts the stored name into the generated support email without HTML encoding, so attackers can make injected HTML and media, such as misleading banners, masked hyperlinks and external tracking resources, render in support messages received by the support team.

Improper removal of sensitive information in the troubleshooting tool in the Amazon ECS MCP Server (awslabs.ecs-mcp-server) before 0.1.36 might allow a remote actor who can influence the agent's input to obtain cleartext container environment variable values and secret references from ECS task definitions, which the server's sensitive data setting is intended to redact, via prompt injection that causes the agent to request troubleshooting guidance.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 0.1.36 or later and rotate any credentials stored as plaintext task definition environment variables.

The Relevanssi – A Better Search plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.28.9. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to use the found_posts count in the JSON response as a boolean exact-match oracle to confirm specific post meta key/value pairs and enumerate which published posts carry a given meta key, including private underscore-prefixed meta such as API keys, tokens, and plugin configuration secrets.

The Premmerce Brands for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'product_brand' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.16 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit is reachable by unauthenticated visitors because WooCommerce's anonymous checkout AJAX endpoint triggers the save_post action, which the plugin processes without any authentication gate, allowing the attacker-supplied product_brand value to be persisted as a new taxonomy term whose name is later echoed unescaped into an HTML attribute on the publicly accessible Brands page.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 18.0 before 19.4.11, 19.5 before 19.5.9, and 19.6 before 19.6.2 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to send requests to internal network resources due to insufficient validation in repository import.

The WP Job Portal – AI-Powered Recruitment System for Company or Job Board website plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in all versions up to, and including, 2.7.2 This is due to a flaw in `WPJOBPORTALuser::__construct()` where the non-empty guard on the `wpjobportal-socialid` cookie is evaluated against the raw cookie value before `sanitize_key()` is applied — allowing a value composed entirely of characters outside `[a-z0-9_-]` to pass the guard, be reduced to an empty string by `sanitize_key()`, and be used as the literal value in a `WHERE socialid = ''` database query that matches the first portal account whose `socialid` column is empty. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to be bound to an existing WP Job Portal Employer or Jobseeker account, gaining the ability to create, edit, and delete the victim's companies, job listings, resumes, and applications, as well as overwrite the linked WordPress user's first name, last name, and display name via the `saveuser`→`syncWPUserName()` path. Exploitation is viable on virtually all installations because every portal account not registered through the social-login flow retains the default empty `socialid` value; nonce checks on downstream actions such as `savecompany` and `saveuser` do not mitigate this issue because those nonces are minted within the already-hijacked session and validate against the attacker's own subsequent requests. Successful exploitation gives the attacker control of a distinct, already-privileged WP Job Portal Employer / Jobseeker (bound to a specific WordPress user) account; it does not promote the attacker's original account.
