The Everest Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form, Quiz, Survey & Custom Form Builder with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to File Deletion in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.4 This is due to the `delete_entry_files()` function gating file cleanup on a loose `preg_match('/signature_/', $meta_key)` substring check against the entry's meta-key rather than verifying the actual field type, which allows an ordinary Text field whose label begins with "Signature" to generate a qualifying meta-key such as `signature_1` — causing the attacker-controlled value submitted via `everest_forms[form_fields][<field_id>]` to be stored verbatim and later passed to `wp_delete_file()`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete files within the `wp-content/uploads/` directory on the server, as `safe_delete_file()` enforces a realpath boundary that prevents deletion of files outside that directory such as `wp-config.php`. Exploitation requires an administrator to permanently delete the attacker's submitted entry, as the unauthenticated attacker cannot trigger the deletion themselves; the targeted file must also reside within `wp-content/uploads/`. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Optimole – Optimize Images | Convert WebP & AVIF | CDN & Lazy Load | Image Optimization plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.20 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This vulnerability is only reachable when the plugin's 'Enable generic placeholder color' option is disabled, as only that configuration invokes the build_url() code path that constructs $low_url from attacker-controlled input.

The CodeColorer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 0.12.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that the attacker has already had one prior comment approved from the same name and email pair, as WordPress's comment_previously_approved check auto-approves subsequent comments from recognized commenters.

The Lightbox with PhotoSwipe plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.18.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires an administrator to approve the attacker's comment at least once, which is the default WordPress behavior for first-time commenters; after that initial approval, no further administrative action is needed and the payload fires for any visitor who opens the lightbox on the affected post.

The Easy SwipeBox plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'title attribute of <a> inside an approved comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The plugin's default-enabled image autodetection applies the Swipebox handler to all front-end anchor elements whose href matches an image extension — including those inside approved comments — meaning no non-default configuration is required to expose the attack surface. A first-time commenter's submission is held for moderator approval, but once approved the stored payload executes for any user who clicks the image link.

The GeoDirectory – WP Business Directory Plugin and Classified Listings Directory plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'opentime (any custom field whose field_type has no geodir_custom_field_value_{type} filter — e.g. time, file, images)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.8.207 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The raw payload is returned unescaped by geodir_cf_time() only when the listing is rendered with the value-raw display mode (e.g., via the [gd_post_meta show="value-raw"] shortcode or block), which is required for script execution.

Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS) vulnerability in Apache Allura's ticket tracking tool.



This issue affects Apache Allura: before 1.23.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.23.0, which fixes the issue.

The GeoDirectory – WP Business Directory Plugin and Classified Listings Directory plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'post_content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.8.207 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload survives storage because wp_kses('post') permits data-* attributes and entity-encoded content, while the dangerous HTML-parsing step occurs entirely within the plugin's own frontend JavaScript handler at render time.

The JetFormBuilder — Dynamic Blocks Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'f_body (mapped to post_content via fields_map)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.8.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires that at least one form on the site contains a Calculated Field block, ensuring the calculated.field.js gadget is enqueued on pages where the stored post content is rendered.

The Advanced Form Integration — Connect Forms to 300+ Apps plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'mapped CF7 fields (e.g. target, mkey, payload)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires an administrator to have pre-configured an AFI integration that maps all three ACF action slots (postId, selector, and value) to public form fields via the plugin's 'Use a form field…' option, which is a non-default configuration.

The Everest Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form, Quiz, Survey & Custom Form Builder with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'everest_forms[form_fields][<wysiwyg field id>]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the targeted form to contain a WYSIWYG field with entry storage enabled; while both are default-available, no form with a WYSIWYG field exists on a stock installation, so an administrator must have manually added such a field to a published form.

The Tutor LMS – eLearning and online course solution plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'withdraw_method_field[bank_transfer_withdraw][account_name]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the site to have Marketplace mode with Revenue Sharing and Bank Transfer enabled, and the Minimum Withdrawal Amount set to zero, allowing a pending-instructor Subscriber to submit a withdrawal request carrying the malicious payload.

The RSS Aggregator by Feedzy – Feed to Post, Autoblogging, News & YouTube Video Feeds Aggregator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in versions up to, and including, 5.2.17 due to insufficient restriction on the wp_kses_allowed_html filter callback. The feedzy_wp_kses_allowed_html() method is registered on wp_kses_allowed_html with the loader's default accepted_args=1, so the callback never receives the context-name argument and unconditionally adds <iframe> (with arbitrary src, width, height, frameborder, allowfullscreen and data-* attributes) to the allowed-tag array for every context — including pre_comment_content, which WordPress uses to sanitize comment bodies submitted by users without the unfiltered_html capability. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory use vulnerability in asfrtp_parse_packet() in libavformat/rtpdec_asf.c that allows malicious RTP sources to leak heap contents by supplying an oversized ASF packet length. Attackers controlling an RTSP server with an x-asf-pf payload can set len_off beyond the RTP payload so the ASF demuxer returns stale heap memory as demuxed media data.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in the MXG demuxer's mxg_read_packet() that allows attackers to leak uninitialized heap memory through truncated marker segments. Attackers can supply a crafted MXG file ending in a truncated APP13 segment with a large declared length, causing uninitialized heap contents to be emitted as audio packet payload, for example into remuxed output files.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in modplug_read_header() in libavformat/libmodplug.c that allocates the buffer using max_size instead of sz. When max_size is set to 0, attackers can supply crafted module files that avio_read() copies into a zero-sized buffer, causing memory corruption, crashes, or possible code execution.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an uninitialized memory vulnerability in nist_read_header() in libavformat/nistspheredec.c, where an inverted ff_alloc_extradata() return check leaves the embedded-shorten extradata byte uninitialized. Attackers can supply a crafted NIST SPHERE file declaring pcm,embedded-shorten coding to leak an uninitialized heap byte into copied output or trigger a NULL pointer write on allocation failure.

FFmpeg 8.0 before 9.1 contains an improper URL scheme validation vulnerability in the WHIP muxer that allows malicious WHIP servers to create or truncate local files via the Location header. Attackers can return a file: URL that dispose_session() opens read-write with truncation on teardown, destroying arbitrary user-writable files or redirecting requests to other protocols.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in ogg_buffer_data() in libavformat/oggenc.c because ogg_buffer_page() leaves a full page current after failed allocation. When page allocation fails, a memset with length (size_t)-1 or an overflowing memcpy writes past the segment table, causing heap memory corruption and crashes when writing Ogg output.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an XML injection vulnerability in ttml_write_header() in libavformat/ttmlenc.c that writes stream language metadata unescaped into the xml:lang attribute. Attackers can supply media files, such as Matroska subtitle tracks with crafted Language values, to inject markup into converted TTML documents and alter downstream parsing or rendering.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in the split_planes size check of write_packet() in libavformat/img2enc.c that allows out-of-bounds heap reads. Attackers can supply a crafted input whose rawvideo stream declares very large width and height, remuxed into .y image files, to leak heap memory into output files or crash the application.

RTL8762C MCU developed by Realtek Semiconductor Corporation has an Improper Protection Against Voltage and Clock Glitches vulnerability. Unauthenticated attackers with physical access can use specialized equipment to perform voltage fault injection and bypass SWD debug authentication, thereby accessing protected data and modifying the chip's execution flow.

Since the fix for CVE-2025-64500, Request::getPathInfo() strips the script name from the start of the URL. It does so even when the script name is only the start of a longer path segment. With SCRIPT_NAME set to /index.php, a request to /index.phpadmin gets the path info /admin and is routed like /admin. Encoded spellings such as /index%2Ephpadmin or /%69ndex.phpadmin work too. Before that fix, the path info was admin, which no route matched.

Rules enforced by Symfony are not affected: access_control and firewalls read the same path info as the router. Rules enforced in front of PHP are. The nginx configuration of the Symfony documentation and the .htaccess file of symfony/apache-pack make /index.php/admin unreachable, but they pass /index.phpadmin to the front controller. So a location /admin block in nginx, a <Location /admin> section in Apache, or a CDN or WAF rule on /admin can be bypassed.

The script name is now stripped only when it is followed by /, ? or the end of the URL. A request to /index.phpadmin gets the path info /index.phpadmin.

When Request::getBaseUrl() does not find the script name at the start of the request URI, it looks for it further into the path. This supports web servers that rewrite every URL to a front controller in a subdirectory. The base URL then kept everything before the script name, and the client chooses that part. A request URI starting with // or /\ made the base URL start with a host.

With SCRIPT_NAME=/public/index.php, a request for //evil.example/public/index.php/login is routed to /login, with the base URL //evil.example/public/index.php and the base path //evil.example/public. The URLs generated for that page then point to evil.example:
- links built with path() and the actions of forms, so a login form sends the credentials of the user to evil.example;
- redirects to generated URLs, such as the ones of redirectToRoute();
- assets referenced with a relative path through asset(), so the page can load scripts from evil.example.

The attacker has to make a user follow a crafted link, such as https://app.example//evil.example/public/index.php/login. framework.trusted_hosts does not help, since the host of the request is the real one.

Applications are affected when their front controller is in a subdirectory and the web server sends it URIs that do not start with that directory. A .htaccess file at the root of the project that rewrites every URL to public/ does that, for instance.

Applications are also affected when the web server sets SCRIPT_NAME to the path of the request. Some nginx configurations do that when they send every request to the front controller without fastcgi_split_path_info. php -S does it too, with a router script outside the document root. A request for /\evil.example/index.php then gets the base URL /\evil.example/index.php, which browsers read as a link to evil.example.

The configurations recommended in the Symfony documentation are not affected.

Request::getBaseUrl() now returns an empty base URL when the request URI starts with // or /\.

Most methods of Symfony\Component\Filesystem\Path rely on Path::split(), which takes everything before the first :// as the root of a path. It doesn't check that this prefix is a URI scheme, so the .. segments in that prefix are never resolved. PHP sees a scheme only at the start of a string. So /base/../x://../secret.txt is a plain local path to /secret.txt for PHP, while Path::isBasePath('/base', '/base/../x://../secret.txt') returns true. canonicalize(), join(), makeAbsolute() and makeRelative() are affected the same way.

Some applications check a path built from user input with isBasePath() or canonicalize(), and then open it. They can be made to read or write files outside the expected directory.

On Symfony 6.4 and later, the AssetMapper component builds with Path::join() the path of the files that a remote package references from its CSS. A malicious or compromised package can therefore make importmap:require or importmap:install write a file of its choice outside assets/vendor. For example, the CSS url(../../../../../public/x://shell.php) writes public/x:/shell.php.

A prefix is now a scheme only when PHP would look for a stream wrapper with that name. That is two or more letters, digits, +, - or ., followed by :// at the start of the path. Other prefixes are regular path segments, and the .. segments after them are resolved. Real schemes such as phar://, file://, vfs:// or compress.zlib:// keep working.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in dudaster ECS – Ele Custom Skin for Elementor ele-custom-skin allows Stored XSS.This issue affects ECS – Ele Custom Skin for Elementor: from n/a through 4.3.14.

An out-of-bounds read in the native C BSON decoding extension of the MongoDB Python Driver may allow an unauthenticated party who can supply crafted BSON data to the decoder to cause the application process to terminate. In some configurations, nearby process memory may be included in error messages, which may result in limited unintended disclosure of data.

JobRouter Premium, version 2025.1.11, has a stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Favorites feature. An authenticated user with low privileges can inject JavaScript code that is persistently stored on the server. When other users access the affected page, the code executes in their browsers. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to perform unauthorized actions on behalf of the victim, access sensitive information, or compromise the integrity of their sessions.

Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS) vulnerability in Webba Plugins Webba Booking webba-booking-lite allows Code Injection.This issue affects Webba Booking: from n/a through 6.5.8.

The Xagio SEO & AEO – AI SEO for Google Rankings & AI Visibility plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'REQUEST_URI' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.0.54 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Execution of the injected script requires an administrator to use the plugin's own "Add 301 Redirect" workflow on the attacker's logged 404 row, which causes the entity-laundered double quote to be written into the redirects table and subsequently rendered unescaped in the administrator's browser. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The LA-Studio Element Kit for Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'actions[].data.settings.triggers.scrolling_to_selector' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The elementor_ajax nonce required to reach the handler is printed in elementorCommonConfig on every wp-admin page, making it trivially obtainable by any logged-in Subscriber via /wp-admin/profile.php; although Elementor's attribute escaping is applied at render time, the stored selector value is subsequently passed to jQuery() by the popup frontend script, which re-parses strings beginning with '<' as HTML, bypassing the escaping.

The Strong Testimonials plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'custom textarea field name (admin-configured, e.g. 'wfx_note')' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.22 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the vendor's paid Strong Testimonials: Custom Fields extension (or another plugin hooking wpmtst_default_fields) to be active and an administrator to have added a custom textarea field to a publicly accessible submission form.

The Calculated Fields Form – AI Form Builder for WordPress – Contact, Payment, Quote, Quiz & More plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'x' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.6.0.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. Exploitation requires the WordPress site to have a published form configured with a URL-backed text field (using the predefined url.x attribute) wired through a calculated-field equation that calls set_timeslots(); without this non-default form configuration, the vulnerable sink is unreachable.

The PDF Invoice for WooCommerce + Drag and Drop Template Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 7.2.0 via deserialization of untrusted input . This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP Object. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable software, which means this vulnerability has no impact unless another plugin or theme containing a POP chain is installed on the site. If a POP chain is present via an additional plugin or theme installed on the target system, it may allow the attacker to perform actions like delete arbitrary files, retrieve sensitive data, or execute code depending on the POP chain present. The incomplete remediation in version 7.2.0 applied escape_pdf_note() only to the customer_note path; the billing address path at woocommerce/shortcodes.php:975–978 remains unpatched, and exploitation requires guest checkout to be enabled along with a payment method that transitions orders to on-hold status (such as the stock WooCommerce Direct Bank Transfer option).

Improper sanitization of mixed data and markup elements when processing content in Kiro Web before 2026-10-30, in combination with agents running specific models such as DeepSeek v3.2, GLM-5, MiniMax M2.1, MiniMax M2.5, or Qwen3-coder-next, may allow a remote unauthenticated actor to execute arbitrary commands in a subscriber's hosted development environment via crafted content being repeated back to the user by the agent.



AWS has addressed this issue. No customer action is required.

DeepSpeed _get_zero_stage Deserialization of Untrusted Data Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of DeepSpeed. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of checkpoint data. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in deserialization of untrusted data. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-29242.

BusyBox ftpd Directory Traversal Arbitrary File Read and Write Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to create or delete arbitrary files or disclose sensitive information on affected installations of BusyBox. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the ftpd service, which listens on TCP port 21 by default. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied path prior to using it in file operations. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to create or delete files or disclose information in the context of the service account. Was ZDI-CAN-27555.

A flaw was found in the Keycloak Operator. Deterministic hashes derived from Kubernetes Secrets are published in generated StatefulSet metadata and in KeycloakOIDCClient status. A user with read access to those resources may be able to recover a low-entropy credential referenced by a Secret, even when Kubernetes RBAC denies the user access to the Secret itself.

The Nexter Extension – Security, Performance, Code Snippets & Site Toolkit plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the site administrator to have enabled the plugin's SEO module (available via a persistent admin notice), after which the nofollow_comments option is on by default; with comments open, a single unauthenticated POST to wp-comments-post.php is sufficient to plant the payload.

The GeoDirectory – WP Business Directory Plugin and Classified Listings Directory plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.8.208 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that at least one prior comment from the attacker's email address has been manually approved, which under WordPress's default comment_previously_approved=1 setting causes subsequent comments from that address to be auto-approved without moderation.

The GeoDirectory – WP Business Directory Plugin and Classified Listings Directory plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'stype' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.8.208 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. This is possible because the plugin's mu-plugin companion (copied automatically on install when the default 'Enable Fast AJAX' option is on) defines DOING_AJAX on any front-end request carrying gd-ajax=1, and an unconditional branch in geodir_get_current_posttype() restores the attacker-controlled stype value after the allow-list check clears it, allowing the tainted value to reach the SQL sink without any preparation.

psqlODBC read memory it had not written, or memory past the end of an application buffer, and sent it to the server or returned it to the application:

- Text bound as SQL_C_CHAR to a large-object parameter was read past the end of the application's buffer, and the extra bytes were stored in the large object.
- After a fetch truncated a long bytea or large-object value, positioned updates and inserts read past the bound buffer and wrote that memory into the row.
- Hex text with a NUL byte, bound to a binary parameter with an explicit length, sent uninitialised heap memory as the parameter value.
- With RowVersioning=1, SQLColumns() on a table that does not exist returned uninitialised stack memory as the schema and table names.
- With UseDeclareFetch=1, bookmarks of updatable block cursors contained uninitialised heap memory, and a malformed ctid from the server sent stale heap bytes in positioned updates and deletes.
- With UseServerSidePrepare=0, calling SQLNumResultCols(), SQLDescribeCol() or SQLColAttribute() on a prepared statement before SQLExecute() read the application's bound parameter buffers and sent their current contents to the server as literals, although ODBC lets the application fill those buffers after the describe.
- The driver named the prepared statements, savepoints, cursors and keyset plans it creates on the server after the heap addresses of its own objects, so the server, or anyone reading an unencrypted connection, learned exact heap addresses inside the client.

Depending on the case, an end user who supplies a parameter value, a database user who stores a long value in a row, or a hostile server can obtain memory of the application process, which may hold data of other users or credentials.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

To escape a bound parameter, or a name passed to a catalog function, psqlODBC has to know where each multibyte character of the client encoding ends. It treated a client encoding named by an alias the server accepts, such as WIN950, Windows950 or big-5 for BIG5, as single-byte, and it accepted too narrow a range of lead bytes for JOHAB, EUC_TW, EUC_CN and EUC_KR. A quote byte that the server reads as part of such a character was then not doubled, or a quote the server reads on its own was taken for part of a character, and the literal ended early.

An end user who controls one bound character parameter, or a name the application passes to a catalog function such as SQLTables(), can run SQL with the rights of the application's database role. This requires a connection that is not in UTF-8: the ANSI driver, or the ANSI entry points, with one of these client encodings. For bound parameters the driver must also be substituting parameters itself, as it does with UseServerSidePrepare=0 or a cursor type other than forward-only.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

To build positioned updates and to describe columns, psqlODBC matches the names in a statement against the catalog. Where it matched differently from the server, it used another table or column:

- Table and schema names were compared case-insensitively in its column-information cache, so users could be taken for another user's "Users", and the driver then evaluated that table's column default to answer @@IDENTITY.
- In FROM ONLY t, ONLY was taken for the table name.
- Column names were compared case-insensitively, so with Parse=1 the type of another column could decide the size of the application's buffer, which a fetch then overflowed.
- In a database whose encoding is single-byte, such as LATIN1 or SQL_ASCII, the server folds the accented letters of an unquoted name by its own locale, while the driver folded only A-Z, so ÉTAT could be taken for another user's "État" instead of état.
- On systems other than Windows, in a Turkish or Azeri locale, an unquoted I was not folded to i, and keywords and ODBC function names did not match.
- Without a schema name, SQLSpecialColumns() could report the key columns of another user's same-named temporary table, and SQLPrimaryKeys() could take another user's index named <table>_pkey for the primary key of a table without one.
- After search_path changed other than through a plain SET statement, positioned writes went to the same-named table in the previously current schema.
- SQLBulkOperations() trusted the ctid stored inside a variable-length bookmark handed back by the application, and ignored the WHERE clause that restricted the cursor, so a forged bookmark read, updated or deleted any row of the cursor's table.

A database user who can create a table in a schema on another user's search_path can redirect that user's positioned updates, inserts and deletes to a table of their choosing, where they run with the victim's rights, or run an expression of their choosing under the victim's role.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC scans statement text itself to substitute parameters, translate ODBC escapes, join batched statements and rewrite queries for updatable cursors. Where it read the text differently from the server, text the driver took for data ran as SQL, or a positioned write went to another table:

- An escape string constant written e'…' in lower case was not recognised as one, and '…' after a keyword ending in E, as in LIKE'…', was taken for one.
- A } inside a quoted literal ended an ODBC {d …}, {t …}, {ts …} or {escape …} sequence.
- Dollar-quote tags containing _ were not recognised, and an identifier starting with _ followed by $, such as _$$, was taken for the start of a dollar quote, so a parameter marker inside a literal was substituted.
- A trailing -- comment in one statement of a batched parameter array swallowed the next statement.
- Comments, literals longer than 255 bytes and escape strings were misread when the driver located the FROM and WHERE clauses of a query for an updatable cursor, and the text copied into the cursor's own queries could include SQL from inside a literal.
- A table name containing $ was cut at the $, and a quoted table name starting with , or ; ended the table list, so positioned updates, inserts and deletes went to another table.
- An integer parameter with an embedded NUL byte cut the query short.
- /*/ was taken for a comment that opens and closes, while the server reads it as one that only opens.
- ConnSettings was split at every semicolon, including one inside a quoted literal, so an application that puts an end user's value into a SET command there ran the rest of the value as SQL at connect time.

An end user who controls text the application puts into a statement, or a parameter value, can run SQL with the rights of the application's database role. A database user who can create a table with a crafted name can redirect another user's positioned writes to a table of their choosing.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC frees memory that is still in use, frees it twice, or writes outside an application buffer in these cases:

- The clean-up the driver runs at commit and rollback sends queries of its own, and the reply to one of them can start the clean-up again while it is running. The nested run frees the rollback log, or the list of cursors and prepared statements to close, and the outer run uses and frees it again.
- The callback through which libpq delivers notices could run that clean-up, and close the connection, while libpq was still using the connection.
- Freeing a statement whose result holds several cursors (FetchRefcursors=1, or UseDeclareFetch=1) used the freed first result while the later cursors were closed.
- With UseDeclareFetch=1, after a rollback closed an updatable cursor, rows added or deleted through it were counted but not stored, so freeing the statement freed uninitialised pointers, and adding a row wrote past the keyset.
- After a multi-row fetch failed on a row other than the first of its rowset, SQLGetData() wrote at an offset past the buffer the application passed.
- SQLProcedureColumns() freed the result of its catalog query twice when the query failed.
- In a process named sqlservr (SQL Server linked servers), a server version below 8.4 made the statement parser free a buffer twice.
- A failed SQLPutData in the middle of a SQLSetPos() or SQLBulkOperations() data-at-execution sequence left the whole operation pending, with the internal statement still allocated and autocommit silently off, so later statements were rolled back at disconnect. The next positioned update ran the stale callback against a statement that was never executed and dereferenced NULL.

Most of these can be triggered by a hostile or compromised server, or anyone on the network path of a connection that does not use sslmode=verify-full (the default is disable). A database user who can make a statement fail, or who controls the contents of a row the application reads, can trigger the UseDeclareFetch=1 and SQLGetData() cases against an honest server. The demonstrated results are crashes and heap corruption; code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

With the driver's debug log (MyLog) turned on, two paths write the database
password to the log in clear text, both beside a line where the driver's own
redaction masks it as PWD=xxxxx:

- Pressing "Test" in the Windows data source setup dialog (psqlsetup.dll)
  logs the whole connection string, which carries PWD= percent-encoded,
  which is reversible, and any password= or sslpassword= inside pqopt.
- The Unicode connect functions SQLDriverConnectW, SQLConnectW and
  SQLBrowseConnectW log their arguments as they convert them between UTF-16
  and UTF-8, before the masking happens. The ANSI entry points are unaffected.

Turning the log on takes an administrator, and MyLog is off by default. The
exposure is the person who later reads the log, which in practice means a log
attached to a bug report or handed to support. Making that safe is the purpose
of the driver's redaction, and these two sites bypassed it.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC uses sizes and counts without checking their range, or keeps them in types too small for them:

- A row array size of 0, set with SQLSetStmtAttr() or on the ARD, makes SQLSetPos() with SQL_REFRESH write past the bound arrays.
- SQL_DESC_COUNT above 32767 on an APD or IPD writes before the start of a heap buffer.
- A numeric parameter with a negative scale overflows a stack buffer.
- SQLGetData() of a text value of 2 GiB or more into a wide-character buffer computes a wrapped size and overflows the heap.
- The 16-bit reference count and size of the statement parser's column-information cache wrap, which frees a cache entry still in use or overflows the cache, and a statement with more than 32768 columns overflows the parser's field array.
- An updatable cursor that records more than 65535 changes in one transaction wraps the 16-bit capacity of its rollback log, which overflows it and frees it twice.
- A statement with 32769 or more parameter markers overflows a 16-bit parameter count.
- A wide-character string of more than 2 GiB wraps the size of its UTF-8 conversion, which is then written below the start of a heap buffer.
- SQLGetDiagField() and SQLGetDiagFieldW() always stored the five-character SQLSTATE plus its terminator and checked BufferLength only afterwards, overrunning a buffer shorter than six bytes.
- The ANSI SQLSetDescField(SQL_DESC_NAME) on an IPD ignored BufferLength and copied the name with strdup(), reading a name passed as pointer plus length past its end.
- SQLFetchScroll(SQL_FETCH_BOOKMARK) did not check the bookmark it was given, so whoever chooses the bookmark value read out of bounds and crashed the process.
- Four places in the parameter conversion read one byte past the end of a bound character parameter, and one of them rewrote it.
- Binding a date, time or timestamp C value to an SQL_INTEGER or SQL_SMALLINT parameter dereferenced NULL instead of returning the conversion error.

Depending on the case, the values come from the application, from the data or statement text an end user supplies, or from a database user who controls the size of a table or value. The demonstrated results are crashes and heap corruption; code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC parsed and built connection strings in ways that let a value end early:

- In a braced value, such as PWD={…}, a trailing byte 0x7d of a GBK, Big5 or SJIS character was taken for the closing brace.
- A braced value that ended right after an escaped }} was not reported as unterminated, and its contents were parsed as further keywords.
- SQLConnectW(), SQLDriverConnectW() and SQLBrowseConnectW() cut a connection string whose UTF-8 form is longer than 32767 bytes, which changes how the rest of it is parsed.
- On Windows with MSDTC, the password and user name were put into the XA open string without escaping, and the XA library copied each item of that string into a 64-byte stack buffer.
- Percent-encoding a long password wrote one byte past a 4096-byte stack buffer.

An end user who supplies a password, or another value the application puts into the connection string, can set other connection keywords, for example to connect the application to a server of their choosing. The MSDTC case can also overflow a stack buffer in the process that loads the XA library.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

On Windows, when a connection takes part in a distributed transaction, psqlODBC and its XA library open further connections of their own to finish the transaction. These connections did not keep the security settings of the application's connection:

- When the XA library's first connection attempt failed, it tried again with sslmode=allow, even for a data source configured with sslmode=verify-full or verify-ca.
- The connections the driver opens itself ignored every libpq option given through pqopt, such as channel_binding=require, and the open string it registers with MSDTC carried no pqopt, so the XA library's connections dropped those options too.

An attacker on the network path between the MSDTC host and the PostgreSQL server, without a certificate or credentials, can make those connections go to a server of their choosing without TLS, read and change what they send, and decide the outcome MSDTC records for the transaction.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC did not check that a server reply matches the query it sent: that a FETCH returns no more rows than it asked for, that each row has the described number of columns, that one query produces one result, and that a COPY, a transaction or the connection ends where the protocol says. By sending replies that do not match, a hostile or compromised server, or anyone on the network path of a connection that does not use sslmode=verify-full (the default is disable) can corrupt memory in the application:

- A FETCH reply with more rows than requested overflows the row cache.
- Extra results in reply to a FETCH, or to the queries of a keyset-driven cursor, are freed while still in use.
- A key query of a keyset-driven cursor answered with extra columns, or a re-read row with fewer columns, overflows the row cache.
- Replies without columns or rows, or with NULL values, to the driver's internal queries at connect time and in catalog functions are dereferenced.
- A malformed relacl value in SQLTablePrivileges() makes the driver write past a buffer.
- On Windows with MSDTC, a long transaction name returned by the server overflows a buffer during recovery.
- Values in replies to the driver's internal queries are used without checking their range: an empty column name, a parameter count, a large-object size, a function's or trigger's argument count, and a result of exactly 32767 columns. They are dereferenced, read past, returned to the application or sent back to the server as stack memory, or make the driver loop forever.
- A reply that ends a COPY, the connection or the transaction at an unexpected point leaves freed results, keysets or table information in use: a CopyOutResponse followed by a lost connection, a ROLLBACK command tag under UseDeclareFetch=1, or a lost connection while a cursor with positioned updates is closed. Eight extra bytes in a reply also make the driver wait forever for a COPY to end.
- On Windows, a start-up reply without client_encoding crashes the driver, and with MSDTC a failed connection makes the XA library use a connection it has already freed.
- An error message ending in the first byte of a multibyte character leaves the SQLSTATE returned by SQLGetDiagRecW() unterminated.
- When a string value did not fit the application's buffer, eight Unicode entry points filled the buffer and wrote no null terminator, so a caller that reads to the terminator, as ODBC allows, read past the end of its own buffer.

This continues the fixes for CVE-2026-120058 and CVE-2026-120060, which covered other replies. The demonstrated results are crashes and heap corruption; code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

A parameter-array execution that fails part-way leaves the rows it has already
queued on the statement handle, and the next execution on that handle sends
them. After a data-at-execution batch is abandoned, by SQLCancel or a
rejected SQLPutData, the next SQLExecDirect sends the failed batch's rows
and returns SQL_SUCCESS without sending its own statement.

So an application that logs the failure on the same handle has its log entry
turned into a silent no-op, while rows it was told had failed are stored. An
end user who controls one value in an application's array insert can arrange
both halves of that.

A second route needs no data-at-execution parameter: when building a later row
fails in parameter conversion, the queued rows go to the server ahead of the
next parameter array on the handle, inside whatever transaction and session
settings are current by then. One variant also writes past the end of a shorter
SQL_ATTR_PARAM_STATUS_PTR array supplied by the next statement.

The statements that run are the application's own, correctly quoted; no SQL
text comes from outside.

Versions from psqlODBC 12.02.0000, which introduced batched parameter-array
execution, up to and including 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC mapped an SSLmode value in a connection string that it did not recognise, such as SSLmode=Require, SSLmode=Verify-Full, SSLmode={require} or SSLmode={verify-full}, to disable. SQLDriverConnect() then returned SQL_SUCCESS with no diagnostic, and the connection was not encrypted.

An attacker on the network path of such a connection can read and change its traffic.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

With SQL_C_DEFAULT, the C type of a bound column or parameter follows its SQL type. An application sizes its buffer from the type it was told when it described the statement. When the column had another type at fetch time, because the server reported another type, the table was altered, or an output parameter's result column had another type, psqlODBC wrote the larger type into the smaller buffer: 12 bytes past a 4-byte buffer for a uuid, and more in multi-row fetches, where the driver also steps through the array by the larger size.

Other conversions wrote past the application's buffer as well:

- With Int8As set to a smaller type, an int8 column fetched as SQL_C_DEFAULT was still written as 8 bytes.
- An int2vector column fetched as SQL_C_DEFAULT returned unterminated binary data instead of text.
- An output parameter that the application discards by binding a NULL buffer overflowed a stack buffer in the driver.
- SQLGetData() with BufferLength 0 on a column the driver reads as a large object wrote a NUL byte past the buffer.
- Adding a row with SQLBulkOperations(SQL_ADD) on a static updatable cursor before the first fetch, then changing that row, rolling back and fetching it, made the keyset index arithmetic free a pointer that was never allocated and corrupt the heap.

This can be triggered by a hostile or compromised server, or anyone on the network path of a connection that does not use sslmode=verify-full (the default is disable), and by the owner of a table the application reads.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

When Debug or CommLog is enabled and the log directory cannot be used, psqlODBC falls back to a directory under the user's home directory. It wrote that path with an unexpanded ~, which is resolved relative to the process's current directory. Another local user who controls a directory on that path can make the driver create the victim's mylog_*.log and psqlodbc_*.log files in any directory the victim can write to, or leave the victim's process blocked in open().

This completes the fix for CVE-2026-120066 in 18.00.0006.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC assumed that a table it reads keeps the definition it had when the statement was described or parsed. A database user who owns a table or view another user's application reads can crash that application, with an honest server and default options, in these cases:

- Columns dropped or added in another session while the application updates rows through an updatable cursor, or describes the columns with Parse=1.
- A view whose ctid is NULL, read through an updatable cursor, which writes past the row cache, and a view with a volatile filter scrolled backward with UseDeclareFetch=1.
- Rows added through an updatable cursor to a table with child tables or partitions.
- A column whose type is named lo, written with data-at-execution parameters.
- A DROP TABLE or ALTER TABLE on the connection while another statement still uses the table's column information.
- NULL key columns in rows the driver re-reads for an updatable cursor.
- A function called with more output parameters than its result has columns.
- SQLTables() and SQLTablesW() dereferenced NULL when called with empty strings for the catalog, schema and table names together with a NULL TableType, which kills the process that loaded the driver and every session it serves.

The demonstrated results are crashes; one case writes past a heap buffer, but code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC rewrites statement text for keyset-driven cursors and ODBC escapes using positions it found in the text. These positions could lie outside the text or describe another statement:

- After SQLExecDirect() failed on a statement handle, the FROM and WHERE positions of the failed statement were applied to the next, shorter statement on that handle.
- The parser could record a FROM position with no text after it, and the rewrite then copied a negative length.
- An {fn …} escape whose arguments contain FOR UPDATE, ; or INTO … FROM made the driver remove a cursor prefix from the wrong buffer.
- {fn CONVERT(?, …)} with an output parameter produced a negative argument length.
- An unclosed {fn …} escape made the driver read past the statement, and a few thousand nested ones exhausted the stack.
- Translating @@identity in long statement text read an uninitialised pointer, and {? = call …} with nothing bound for the return value dereferenced NULL.

Whoever supplies the text of a statement that an application opens on a keyset-driven or dynamic cursor with a concurrency other than read-only, or calls with an output parameter, can corrupt the application's heap and end it. That includes the users of query tools, report builders and other applications that run SQL their users type. Code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

The UsersWP – Front-end login form, User Registration, User Profile & Members Directory plugin for WP plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the '<htmlvar_name> of any editor-type Account field (e.g. about_work)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.83 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that an administrator has configured at least one editor-type Account field with public visibility and directory display enabled, as no such field exists in a default installation.

The Advanced Product Fields (Product Addons) for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'wapf[field_<id>]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload survives sanitization via a whitespace-prefixed tag gadget, is normalized into real HTML elements by wp_kses_post() and force_balance_tags() at render time, and is then executed by WordPress core's tags-box.js when it encounters the forged #tagsdiv-post_tag element on the order screen.

The Classified Listing – AI-Powered Classified ads & Business Directory plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'formData[description]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.3.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload survives server-side sanitization because wp_kses_post permits span elements with class and data-* attributes; script execution is triggered only when a privileged user (Administrator or Editor) clicks the .reveal-phone span on the pending listing's preview page, causing rtcl-public.js to pass the attacker-controlled data-options value directly into jQuery.append. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Essential Real Estate plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'property_des' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.3.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with custom-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The plugin's own initialization migration automatically promotes Subscriber-level users to the ere_customer role, and with the default auto_publish=1 setting, the malicious property is immediately published and visible to any visitor or administrator who opens it.

The GD bbPress Tools plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'signature' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.0.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The crafted signature payload is stored verbatim in user meta and fires when an Administrator views the attacker's topic on the Edit Topic admin screen.

The GeoDirectory – WP Business Directory Plugin and Classified Listings Directory plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'post_content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.8.208 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires an administrator to have previously configured a Shortcode-type tab whose template places %%post_content%% inside an HTML attribute, which is not a default configuration; unauthenticated exploitation additionally requires the plugin's 'Allow posting without logging in?' option and WordPress user registration to both be enabled.

The Pixeline’s Email Protector plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the malicious comment to pass the site's moderation queue, which WordPress enforces for first-time commenters by default but which does not re-sanitize stored comment content.

GNU Inetutils FTP Client File Retrieval Command Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of GNU Inetutils FTP Client. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must interact with a malicious FTP server.

The specific flaw exists within the processing of filenames. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to execute a system call. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current user. Was ZDI-CAN-29119.

GNU Inetutils talkd Stack-based Buffer Overflow Denial-of-Service Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to create a denial-of-service condition on affected installations of GNU Inetutils. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the processing of announce requests. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a fixed-length stack-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to create a denial-of-service condition on the system. Was ZDI-CAN-29120.

Pydantic AI Harness's PlaywrightBrowser applies an egress policy to the requests a page makes. It treated any URL containing a backslash as having no host, and it allows script and asset requests with no host. A page script could therefore add a backslash to a URL's query to send requests to private addresses, to hosts outside allowed_domains, and to hosts in blocked_domains.

This affects applications that use PlaywrightBrowser to open pages or follow instructions an attacker can influence. It applies to fetch, XHR, sendBeacon, WebSocket and passive asset requests. Navigation and frames were not affected. A policy that limits every request kind to an allowlist did not prevent data from being sent to another host.

Responses from private services could be read only when the service permits cross-origin reads or accepts the WebSocket connection. Current Chromium versions separately block many requests from public pages to private addresses, but not requests between public hosts, and not when the browser runs behind a forward proxy.

The assumed attacker is a third party with no access to the application who controls script on a page the agent opens, or content that steers the agent's browser tools.

Upgrade pydantic-ai-harness to 0.74.0 or later. Until then, enforce egress outside the browser with a firewall or a filtering proxy, and do not rely on the browser's domain lists for untrusted pages.

Pydantic AI Harness's PlaywrightBrowser enforces its egress policy on HTTP requests and page WebSockets, but not on WebRTC or WebTransport connections, WebSockets opened with WebSocketStream, or the requests the browser itself sends for FedCM. A page the agent opens can make the browser send WebRTC (STUN and TURN), WebTransport and WebSocketStream traffic, and FedCM requests, to hosts and ports that the policy refuses, including under a policy that limits every request kind to an allowlist.

This affects applications that use PlaywrightBrowser to open pages an attacker can influence. The traffic is each protocol's connection setup, sent to a destination the page chooses. A page can learn whether a target answers a STUN request. No response body from an ordinary internal service was readable through WebRTC, WebTransport or FedCM. A WebSocketStream is an ordinary WebSocket that the WebSocket guard does not see, opened from a page, a frame or a worker, and the page reads what the server sends, including from a private address. Chromium's Local Network Access blocks WebTransport from public pages to private addresses, but does not block WebRTC.

A FedCM call (navigator.credentials.get with an identity provider) makes the browser fetch the provider's /.well-known/web-identity, config, accounts and client metadata URLs. The page chooses the config URL's path and the client ID, so it can send data to a host outside allowed_domains or listed in blocked_domains. The accounts request carries the provider's cookies from the browser profile. FedCM requires a provider origin that is HTTPS or loopback.

The assumed attacker is a third party with no access to the application who controls script on a page the agent opens.

Under an enforced egress policy, which is the default, pydantic-ai-harness 0.74.0 removes RTCPeerConnection, webkitRTCPeerConnection, WebTransport, WebSocketStream, IdentityCredential and IdentityProvider from every page and frame, refuses FedCM calls to navigator.credentials.get, and launches Chromium with FedCM and WebSocketStream turned off. These paths stay outside the policy: WebTransport from workers; WebSocketStream from workers in a browser reached over cdp_url; WebTransport in sandboxed iframes that Chromium runs in their own process (headless=False and cdp_url); and documents loaded before attachment under cdp_context='default'.

Upgrade pydantic-ai-harness to 0.74.0 or later. For the paths the upgrade leaves open, and until you upgrade, run the browser behind a network egress filter that also covers UDP, or do not open untrusted URLs with PlaywrightBrowser.

An authenticated attacker may then gain access to areas or business roles they are not authorized to use, or obtain unauthorized permissions in Panorama. Installations that do not use POSIX LDAP authentication are not affected. LDAP Active Directory authentication is not affected.



Affected versions:

  *  Panorama Suite 2020
  *  Panorama Suite 2022-SP1
  *  Panorama Suite 2023
  *  Panorama Suite 2025
  *  Panorama Suite 2025 Updated Dec. 25 (before update PS-2510-02-1317)




Remediation: For Panorama Suite 2025 Updated Dec. 25, install update PS-2510-02-1317 or later. For the other affected versions, upgrade to Panorama Suite 2025 Updated Dec. 25 and install update PS-2510-02-1317 or later.



Please refer to security bulletin BS-040 on the Panorama CSIRT website:  https://my.codra.net/en-gb/csirt .

Crypt::JWT versions before 0.037_1 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded inflation of zip DEF payloads.

When a token header sets "zip" to "DEF", decode_jwt inflates the payload with no limit on the output size. A signed token is inflated after its signature verifies. An encrypted token is inflated after decryption, and with RSA-OAEP or ECDH-ES key management anyone who holds the recipient's public key can produce a token that decrypts.

Crypt::JWT versions before 0.037_1 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via an unbounded PBES2 iteration count.

For a token using a PBES2 key management algorithm, decode_jwt passes the p2c header parameter to PBKDF2 as the iteration count without a range check, and derives the key before any integrity check. Unless accepted_alg rules it out, a token can select PBES2 whenever decode_jwt is given a symmetric key.

A vulnerability was found in GL.iNet GL-A1300, GL-AR300M, GL-AR300M16, GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-B3000, GL-BE3600, GL-BE6500, GL-BE9300, GL-BE10000, GL-BE14000, GL-E750, GL-E750V2, GL-E5800, GL-MT300N-V2, GL-MT1300, GL-MT2500, GL-MT2500A, GL-MT3000, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000, GL-MT6000, GL-SFT1200, GL-X300B, GL-X750, GL-X750V2, GL-X2000, GL-X3000, GL-XE300 and GL-XE3000. This impacts the function ovpn-client.set_group of the file /rpc of the component Management RPC. The manipulation results in null pointer dereference. The attack can be executed remotely. Upgrading the affected component is recommended. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

A vulnerability was determined in GL.iNet GL-A1300, GL-AR300M, GL-AR300M16, GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-B3000, GL-BE3600, GL-BE6500, GL-BE9300, GL-BE10000, GL-BE14000, GL-E750, GL-E750V2, GL-E5800, GL-MT300N-V2, GL-MT1300, GL-MT2500, GL-MT2500A, GL-MT3000, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000, GL-MT6000, GL-SFT1200, GL-X300B, GL-X750, GL-X750V2, GL-X2000, GL-X3000, GL-XE300 and GL-XE3000. Affected is the function plugins.get_package_info of the file /rpc of the component Management RPC. This manipulation causes null pointer dereference. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

A vulnerability was identified in GL.iNet GL-A1300, GL-AR300M, GL-AR300M16, GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-B3000, GL-BE3600, GL-BE6500, GL-BE9300, GL-BE10000, GL-BE14000, GL-E750, GL-E750V2, GL-E5800, GL-MT300N-V2, GL-MT1300, GL-MT2500, GL-MT2500A, GL-MT3000, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000, GL-MT6000, GL-SFT1200, GL-X300B, GL-X750, GL-X750V2, GL-X2000, GL-X3000, GL-XE300 and GL-XE3000. Affected by this vulnerability is the function plugins.install_package of the file /rpc of the component Management RPC. Such manipulation leads to null pointer dereference. The attack may be performed from remote. Upgrading the affected component is advised. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

A security flaw has been discovered in GL.iNet GL-A1300, GL-AR300M, GL-AR300M16, GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-B3000, GL-BE3600, GL-BE6500, GL-BE9300, GL-BE10000, GL-BE14000, GL-E750, GL-E750V2, GL-E5800, GL-MT300N-V2, GL-MT1300, GL-MT2500, GL-MT2500A, GL-MT3000, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000, GL-MT6000, GL-SFT1200, GL-X300B, GL-X750, GL-X750V2, GL-X2000, GL-X3000, GL-XE300 and GL-XE3000. Affected by this issue is the function plugins.set_config of the file /rpc of the component Management RPC. Performing a manipulation results in null pointer dereference. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. It is advisable to upgrade the affected component. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

A weakness has been identified in GL.iNet GL-A1300, GL-AR300M, GL-AR300M16, GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-B3000, GL-BE3600, GL-BE6500, GL-BE9300, GL-BE10000, GL-BE14000, GL-E750, GL-E750V2, GL-E5800, GL-MT300N-V2, GL-MT1300, GL-MT2500, GL-MT2500A, GL-MT3000, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000, GL-MT6000, GL-SFT1200, GL-X300B, GL-X750, GL-X750V2, GL-X2000, GL-X3000, GL-XE300 and GL-XE3000. This affects the function wg-client.add_config of the file /rpc of the component Management RPC. Executing a manipulation can lead to null pointer dereference. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. You should upgrade the affected component. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

A security vulnerability has been detected in GL.iNet GL-A1300, GL-AR300M, GL-AR300M16, GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-B3000, GL-BE3600, GL-BE6500, GL-BE9300, GL-BE10000, GL-BE14000, GL-E750, GL-E750V2, GL-E5800, GL-MT300N-V2, GL-MT1300, GL-MT2500, GL-MT2500A, GL-MT3000, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000, GL-MT6000, GL-SFT1200, GL-X300B, GL-X750, GL-X750V2, GL-X2000, GL-X3000, GL-XE300 and GL-XE3000. This vulnerability affects the function wg-client.set_config of the file /rpc of the component Management RPC. The manipulation leads to null pointer dereference. The attack can be initiated remotely. The affected component should be upgraded. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

Open Babel through 3.2.1 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in OBForceField::Setup() that leaves stored constraints bound to freed atoms when set up with an empty molecule. Attackers can supply a molecule file yielding an empty molecule so later SteepestDescent() or ConjugateGradients() calls read freed memory, causing crashes or incorrect results.

libyang through 6.4.13 contains a release of invalid pointer vulnerability in ly_in_memory() and ly_in_memory_chunk() in src/in.c that return the current read position instead of the previous start address. Attackers supplying YANG data parsed from a heap buffer can cause applications freeing the returned pointer to pass an interior address to free(), aborting the process.

Paid Memberships Pro before 3.8.8 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read restricted post excerpts because restriction is reapplied only through the_excerpt filter. Attackers can request RSS or Atom feeds, oEmbed URLs, or pages rendering the Post Excerpt block to read opening text or manual excerpts of member-only posts.

Part-DB (Part-DB-server) before 2.20.6 contains an open redirect vulnerability in several controllers that pass user-supplied _redirect or redirect_back parameters to redirect() without validating local paths. Attackers can craft links to endpoints like /tools/batch_eda_edit using scheme-relative or protocol-relative values that bypass the nelmio_security guard, sending authenticated victims to attacker-controlled phishing sites.

nconf through 1.0.0-beta.2 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in the Memory store merge() function in lib/nconf/stores/memory.js that lacks __proto__ key rejection. Attackers controlling merge keys like '__proto__:isAdmin' or nested __proto__ properties can inject properties into Object.prototype, altering application logic or causing errors.

A vulnerability was determined in FastStone Image Viewer up to 8.5. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file FSViewer.exe of the component ICO Decoder. Executing a manipulation can lead to out-of-bounds write. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was identified in philipjscott simple-thumbnail up to 1.6.5. This issue affects the function ffmpegExecute of the file index.js. The manipulation of the argument seek leads to os command injection. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A security flaw has been discovered in msaifulcsse Ticket-Travel-Management-System 28b68cea41b3a9eb8d533db992e0b5ba2db68854/15c7bc0b48c263233326bb227fef01efc54c24a7. Impacted is an unknown function of the file bus1.php. The manipulation of the argument dfrom/gto/ddate/rdate results in sql injection. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. This product takes the approach of rolling releases to provide continious delivery. Therefore, version details for affected and updated releases are not available. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A weakness has been identified in nliautaud pico-content-editor up to 02d5ad6c820c5050c542ab9505819b5e0a0ba1af. The affected element is the function getLanguageContent of the file src/EditorsHandlers/ContentTools.php of the component ContentTools Editor. This manipulation of the argument ContentToolsUrl causes server-side request forgery. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. Continious delivery with rolling releases is used by this product. Therefore, no version details of affected nor updated releases are available. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way. This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

A security vulnerability has been detected in Ghostty up to 1.3.1. The impacted element is an unknown function of the component macOS OSC 8 Hyperlink Handler. Such manipulation leads to injection. The attack can be launched remotely. Upgrading to version 1.4.0 is sufficient to resolve this issue. The name of the patch is 54fe8e188552977249a084db687e75aee6bf12e9. Upgrading the affected component is advised.

A vulnerability has been found in TAILG Feimeng up to 20261028. Affected is an unknown function of the component Wireless Remote Control System. The manipulation leads to authentication bypass by capture-replay. The attack needs to be initiated within the local network. The attack is considered to have high complexity. The exploitability is told to be difficult. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A weakness has been identified in Spotweb up to 1.5.8. This issue affects the function redirect of the file lib/SpotTemplateHelper.php of the component Login. Executing a manipulation of the argument http_referer can lead to open redirect. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. This patch is called 0853d646d615225b35f466a960976d1492b786a9. Applying a patch is advised to resolve this issue.

A flaw was found in bootc. On a sealed composefs boot with a strict composefs digest on the kernel command line, the initramfs derives fs-verity enforcement from unsigned repository metadata and can mount an image under images/refs without measuring it against that digest. An attacker with offline write access to the root filesystem can boot a modified root under a legitimately signed UKI.

A flaw was found in bootc. On a sealed composefs boot, a failed bootc-root-setup.service does not fail initrd-root-fs.target, so the initramfs can switch root into the unverified physical root under the original signed UKI.

A security vulnerability has been detected in TOTOLINK N350RT 9.3.5u.6468_B20250827/9.3.5u.6466_B20250825. The affected element is the function setLanguageCfg of the file /cgi-bin/cstecgi.cgi. Such manipulation of the argument lang leads to authorization bypass. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used.

A vulnerability was detected in mahmoudai1 school-management-system up to ecec9faaf2fb1a3c5cd096e063f8ef326d09cdfd. The impacted element is the function userModel::checkUserInDB of the file loginServer.php of the component Login Handler. Performing a manipulation of the argument ID results in sql injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

DeepSeek-Reasonix before 2.53.0 contains a command execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run commands without user approval because the shellsafe classifier treats git blame and git whatchanged as read-only. Attackers can plant a diff textconv driver in .gitattributes and .git/config so that git blame, triggered via prompt injection or routine use, executes attacker-chosen commands with the user's privileges, exposing stored provider API keys and session history.

llama.cpp from b7118 before b12604 contains an integer underflow vulnerability in llama_grammar_parser::parse_sequence() that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to cause denial of service by supplying GBNF repetitions with max lower than min. Attackers can send a grammar like {5,2} in the grammar field of a llama-server /completion request, wrapping n_opt to generate endless repetition rules that hang the process and exhaust memory.

Cron-parser through 5.10.0 contains an unbounded memory allocation vulnerability in CronExpressionParser.parse() that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory by supplying oversized cron fields. Attackers can submit a roughly 1.6 MB expression of repeated wildcard tokens that expand into huge arrays, exhausting the V8 heap and crashing the Node.js process.

ToolJet from 3.16.0 before 3.20.256 contains an improper signature verification vulnerability in StripeWebhookGuard that validates webhooks against a self-generated signature instead of the Stripe-Signature header. Unauthenticated attackers can post forged Stripe events to the POST /api/organization/payment/webhooks route to activate subscriptions, generate licenses, change plans or seats, and add AI credits without payment.

paramz through 0.10.0 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying crafted model files to paramz.load(), which calls pickle.load() without restrictions. Attackers can embed objects whose __reduce__ method returns callables like exec or os.system in shared paramz or GPy model files to run code with the victim's privileges.

Wallos before 5.11.2 contains an infinite loop vulnerability that allows authenticated users or API key holders to exhaust server resources by storing subscriptions with a frequency of 0. Attackers can trigger renew.php or get_monthly_cost.php to loop forever on a P0D interval, pinning PHP workers and hanging the next-payment cron job for all users.

BookStack before 26.09.3 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated Editors to permanently delete recycle bin content by converting chapters to books or books to shelves. Attackers can trigger TrashCan::destroyEntity() through the conversion actions to force-delete soft-deleted children, revisions and attachments, including content deleted by other users, preventing restoration.

Leptonica 1.79.0 through 1.87.0 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in l_byteaInitFromStream() that allows attackers to write past a heap buffer by supplying oversized input. Attackers can provide a file larger than 1,000,000,000 bytes, causing l_byteaCreate() to allocate a 201-byte buffer before memcpy copies the full stream size, crashing the application.

Chatwoot before 4.20.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the Bandwidth SMS webhook endpoint POST /webhooks/sms/:phone_number that allows unauthenticated attackers to submit forged SMS events. Attackers who know an inbox phone number can set the 'to' field to inject inbound messages with forged sender numbers or forge delivery status updates.

Chatwoot before 4.20.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows account administrators to attach integration hooks to other accounts' inboxes by supplying a foreign inbox_id. Attackers can create a Dialogflow hook referencing a victim inbox, leaving its new conversations stuck as pending awaiting a bot, and enumerate inbox IDs to disclose inbox names.

Loginizer before 2.1.4 contains a brute-force lockout bypass vulnerability in loginizer_login_failed() that allows unauthenticated attackers to avoid failed-attempt recording via non-ASCII URL bytes. Attackers can append invalid UTF-8 or 4-byte sequences to wp-login.php or xmlrpc.php request URLs, causing the log INSERT to fail and enabling unlimited password guessing without lockout or email notification.

GNOME libxml2 2.9.10 through 2.15.4 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmlValidatePopElement because xmlCtxtReset frees the DTD without popping stale validation states. Attackers supplying an XML document ending inside an element to an application reusing a DTD-validating xmlTextReader can trigger heap reads, causing crashes and limited heap disclosure via error messages.
